General statement. lem:robust-sum-affine-hull and cor:robust-pair-moments are deterministic all-parameter statements. prop:two-cover-budget identifies the cost of this sufficient criterion, not a formula upper bound. thm:conditional-modular-sections proves the revised source and conditional sections with their full variable and encoding ledger.

Odd additive order rules out an affine consequence

Let \(K=\mathbb F_q\) have odd characteristic \(p\), let \(F\) be any field of characteristic different from \(p\), and let \(a_i\in K\) be coefficients on a finite Boolean coordinate set \(H\). A coordinate group covers \(K\) when its Boolean subset sums \(\{\sum_i a_ix_i:x_i\in\{0,1\}\}\) equal \(K\). It is \(r\)-robust if it still covers after deleting any at most \(r\) coordinates.

Lemma (robust sum affine hull). Suppose \(H\) contains disjoint groups \(A,B\), each one-robust. For every \(t\in K\), the relation \[R_t=\{x\in\{0,1\}^H:\textstyle\sum_i a_ix_i=t\}\tag{1}\] is nonempty and has full affine hull \(F^H\). Zero coefficients and additional coordinates outside \(A\cup B\) are allowed.

Proof. Let \(f=c+\sum_i b_ix_i\), with coefficients in \(F\), vanish on \(R_t\). First fix all extra coordinates to zero. Every sum \(s\in K\) is attained on \(A\), and a completing assignment of sum \(t-s\) exists on \(B\). Therefore any two assignments on \(A\) with equal modular sum must have the same value of \(\sum_{i\in A}b_ix_i\): compare them with that same completion. Define this common value to be \(u(s)\in F\). The same reasoning defines the corresponding value function on \(B\).

For \(i\in A\), the group \(A\setminus\{i\}\) covers \(K\). Choose an assignment on it of each sum \(s\), then set bit \(i\) to zero or one. The definition of \(u\) gives \[u(s+a_i)-u(s)=b_i\quad(s\in K).\tag{2}\] If \(a_i=0\), this immediately gives \(b_i=0\). Otherwise adding \(a_i\) has order \(p\) in the additive group of \(K\); summing (2) around that orbit gives \(p b_i=0\). Since \(\operatorname{char}F\ne p\), again \(b_i=0\). Similarly all coefficients on \(B\) vanish. Nonemptiness of the zero-extra fibre forces \(c=0\). For each extra coordinate, set it to one and the other extras to zero; the two covering groups still complete to the required target, forcing its coefficient to vanish. Thus \(f=0\), which proves full affine hull. \(\square\)

This is the parity-conditioned subset-sum issue in a form that avoids enumerating parities: over \(\mathbb F_2\), any nonconstant parity omitted by a target fibre would be a nonzero affine vanishing function after adjusting its constant. The odd additive orbit forbids it under the robust-cover hypothesis. Matching proof characteristic is genuinely excluded: the original modular affine equation itself may be a nonzero affine consequence there.

Corollary (robust pair moments). If both groups are three-robust, then after any assignment on at most two further coordinates, every target fibre on the remaining coordinates is nonempty and affine-full over \(F\). Moreover, on every unpinned target fibre the functions \(1,x_i\) and any one selected quadratic \(x_sx_t\), \(s\ne t\), are linearly independent.

Proof. Remove the pinned coordinates from each group. They remain one-robust, and the pinned values only change the modular target, so the lemma applies. If \(c+\sum_i b_ix_i+d x_sx_t\) vanishes, fix each of the four assignments on \(s,t\). The resulting affine function vanishes on an affine-full relation in the other variables, forcing all their coefficients to zero. The four remaining scalar equations then force \(c,b_s,b_t,d\) to zero. This proves the independence and hence surjectivity of the dual moment map. No simultaneous independence of all quadratics is asserted. \(\square\)

The criterion has a real budget cost

Proposition (two-cover budget). A one-robust group covering a field of size \(q\) needs at least \(1+\lceil\log_2q\rceil\) coordinates. In a regular modular incidence system of row width \(k\), a set \(S\) whose every row has two such disjoint groups among its unpinned coordinates must satisfy \[|S|\le v\left(1-\frac{2+2\lceil\log_2q\rceil}{k}\right).\tag{3}\] For the preceding parameters \(v=l2^l,k=8l,q>v^2\), this forces a deficit of order at least \(v\log l/l\) below half. Thus this particular all-row sufficient condition cannot certify the depth-at-least-three near-half budget on that source.

Proof. After deleting one coordinate, at least \(q\) subset sums are needed, so \(2^{|A|-1}\ge q\). If each variable has \(r\) occurrences and there are \(m=rv/k\) rows, the total unpinned row incidence is \(r(v-|S|)\). It is at least \(m(2+2\lceil\log_2q\rceil)\), giving (3). At the old parameters \(\log_2q>2l+2\log_2l\), which yields the stated deficit. This is a limitation of the two-cover proof premise, not a bound on actual PC degree or on actual conditional affine fullness. \(\square\)

A revised source with all-pin conditional sections

For integers \(l\to\infty\), replace the parameters by \[v=l2^l,\quad k=16l,\quad m=9v/k=9\cdot2^{l-4},\quad v^2<q<2v^2,\quad q\text{ prime}.\tag{4}\] Use nine independent uniform labelled partitions into \(k\)-sets, independent uniform supported coefficients in \(\mathbb F_q\), and central targets \(b_a=\frac12\sum_i a_{ai}\). The proof field for the sections below is \(\mathbb F_2\).

Theorem (conditional modular sections). With probability \(1-o(1)\), this source is Boolean-empty, field-consistent with full row rank, has nonzero coefficients and essential rows, and extends all pins through \(d=\lfloor k/64\rfloor\). Every normalized minimal core retains \(n\ge e^{-512}v/256\) actual variables, has essential full-binary-affine rows, between two and nine occurrences, no common Horn polarity, width \(O(\log n)\) and canonical encoding length \(O(n^{17})\). Original rows remain complement-invariant.

On the same event there is a set \(S\) with \[|S|\ge v/2-9v e^{-l/64}\tag{5}\] such that, after every assignment to \(S\), each residual row and each of its additional two-coordinate pin fibres is nonempty and binary affine-full. Every residual overlap moment map of the earlier compatible-selector theorem is onto. Therefore every assignment to \(S\) admits compatible mass-one local coefficient families. They can be chosen with polynomial coefficients depending only on the pinned coordinates of their own row, of degree at most \(k\). These are raw sections, not a degree-D PC certificate.

Uniform robust covers. The all-target subset-sum bound, proved from the full subset fourth moment, says that \(h\) independent uniform coefficients fail to cover \(\mathbb F_q\) with probability at most \[q^4 2^{-3h}+3q^3 2^{-2h}+3q^2(3/8)^h.\tag{6}\] Fix a half set \(S_0\). Call a row bad if \(|X_a\setminus S_0|<\lceil15k/32\rceil\). For each good row, split those outside coordinates as evenly as possible into two groups; for every row also split its entire scope evenly into two groups. All these choices depend only on incidence, not coefficients. Demand coverage after every deletion of at most three coordinates from each group.

In the good-row outside groups, even after those deletions the remaining size is at least \(15l/4-4\). The full-row groups have still more coordinates. There are \(O(mk^3)\) tested subsets, each with independent uniform coefficients conditional on incidence. Union bounding (6), the three terms have exponential factors, up to polynomial factors in \(l\), \[2^{-9l/4},\qquad 2^{-l/2},\qquad [2^5(3/8)^{15/4}]^l.\tag{7}\] The fourth power of the last base is \(3^{15}/2^{25}<1\). Thus all the demanded groups are three-robust with probability \(1-o(1)\). Correlations between overlapping tested subsets do not affect this union bound.

Delete only rare bad-row coordinates. The earlier elementary hypergeometric moment-generating bound applies unchanged. Badness makes the row's selected-coordinate count exceed \(17k/32\), a deviation of \(k/32\) from its mean. Hence its probability is at most \(e^{-k/512}=e^{-l/32}\). Markov's inequality makes the number of bad rows at most \(m e^{-l/64}\), except with probability \(e^{-l/64}\). Remove from \(S_0\) every variable of these rows, giving (5).

For a good row, the two robust groups originally outside \(S_0\) are still free after any pin on the smaller \(S\). Additional unpinned coordinates are allowed by the lemma. For a bad row, no coordinate in its scope lies in \(S\); its two full-row robust groups apply. The robust-pair corollary now proves nonempty affine-full fibres after every pin on \(S\), with up to two additional arbitrary pins, uniformly over all targets. This does not require a union bound over the exponentially many assignments to \(S\).

Overlap maps and explicit sections. The random-partition overlap argument also applies to nine layers: the probability of a triple intersection is \(O(k^4/v)\), and that a row has two distinct double-overlap neighbours is \(O(k^5/v)\). Thus pair overlaps have size at most two and the double-overlap graph is a matching with high probability. Restriction cannot increase these intersections. Each residual row's moment inventory therefore consists of the constant, all its remaining singletons, and at most one quadratic from its double-overlap partner. The robust-pair corollary makes its evaluation functions independent, so the dual map is onto.

For each pin \(u\in\{0,1\}^S\), prescribe mass one and zero for every nonempty residual overlap monomial. Choose a right inverse in each row, obtaining a compatible coefficient family by the proved marginal construction. Since a row's allowed tuples and moment map depend only on \(u|_{S\cap X_a}\), make those choices once for each local pin, not once for each global pin. Embed a row's conditional vector in its fixed original tuple-coordinate space by zero outside its pin fibre. Each coordinate is then a scalar multiple of the indicator of one assignment to \(S\cap X_a\), hence has degree at most \(|S\cap X_a|\le k\). Embed every conditional right inverse in that same fixed original-tuple row space, with the fixed residual-moment columns. Comparing these fixed matrix entries across local pins, the same local interpolation bound applies to each entry. Pointwise multiplication and matrix composition are ordinary Boolean polynomial operations on these coefficient functions.

Source properties and all-core ledger. Field consistency is automatic at all coordinates \(1/2\). Incidence counting gives Hall's condition for a matching saturating the rows once \(k\ge9\); the matching minor is a nonzero degree-m polynomial in the independent coefficients. Rank failure is at most \(m/q\), and zero supported coefficients cost at most \(9v/q\). Every fixed Boolean assignment satisfies each independent central row with probability \(1/q\), so expected Boolean solutions are at most \(2^v/q^m\le2^{-v/8}\).

For uniform pins through \(d\), use the exact zero-coordinate central-slice law on \(k-1\) bits. The existing second-moment extension estimate, unioned over all rows, is at most \[2mq2^{-k}\sum_{j=0}^d\binom kj4^j \le2mq2^{-k}(d+1)(256e)^{k/64} =O(l^3 2^{-21l/2})=o(1),\tag{8}\] using \(e<4\). Complementation transfers pins involving the distinguished coordinate as before. Set \(\beta=255/256\), \(\alpha=e^{-512}\), \(R=\lfloor\alpha v/k\rfloor\). The same labelled-partition counting proof, now with nine layers, bounds each expansion failure at row-set size \(s\le R\) by \[[(9e/\alpha)e^{-k}]^s.\tag{9}\] Summing gives \(o(1)\), so the projection core-retention lemma applies with \(d+1-k/256>3k/256\) and eventually \(R\ge\alpha v/(2k)\). It yields \(n>3\alpha v/512>\alpha v/256\) uniformly over all permitted cores and normalizations.

The full-row robust groups prove original binary affine fullness, which survives all coordinate projections. As already proved, an unsatisfiable collection of nonempty full-affine relations cannot have a common Horn polarity. Nonzero coefficients make the original scopes essential; normalization gives essential terminal scopes and at least two occurrences, while deletion and projection preserve the upper occurrence bound nine. Canonical length is at most \(O(m2^k k\log(v+1))=O(v^{17})\), and hence \(O(n^{17})\) because \(n\ge\alpha v/256\). All variables are counted and no Boolean auxiliaries are added. Terminal degree-D refutations replay on the original through \(\max\{k,D\}\), not conversely. The large set (5) belongs to the original source; no near-half size for its intersection with every normalized core is asserted. \(\square\)

What was gained and what still fails

The alternative source's width changes from \(8l\) to \(16l\), occurrence count from five to nine, and polynomial encoding bound from degree nine to degree seventeen. Original variable count and complement symmetry are unchanged. Field consistency, Boolean emptiness, full row rank, pin extension and all-core retention survive, while all-pin conditional moment surjectivity on a near-half selected set is gained. The fixed-width structural envelope and its guarded width-five witness are unchanged. The new logarithmic-width family is still independent of a proposed proof-size exponent; its complete Frege transfer remains unproved.

The conditional state module over the full Boolean algebra on \(S\) has exponential total dimension, but polynomial-size fibres and pointwise coefficient-linear operators. It is therefore still excluded as a PC certificate by both the dimension and modular-fibre obstructions. The displayed entries have coefficient degrees up to \(k\), not a proved increase of one per variable action. A shifted or truncated filtration must be constructed and checked; arbitrary shifts do not make vector axiom images or kernels correct. The guarded-product counterexample continues to distinguish all-row local extension from joint consequence annihilation.

Follow-up. Continuing, with rotation at the local-section head's four-entry boundary. The spell constructed marginal selectors, proved their exponential dimension requirement and coefficient-module obstruction, and supplied stronger conditional source data, but left the necessary near-half kernel unchanged. No extension is claimed. Keep the degree-filtered transport task queued; return to the next head's global question rather than treating conditional sections as the desired invariant.

Sub-ideas

  • For the revised nine-partition central source, construct a degree-filtered vector map from the raw conditional sections whose kernel is proper and stable under every legal multiplication. Count coefficient degrees and permit global Booleanity or coefficient commutation to fail beyond the legal window. The pointwise full-module maps are already excluded, and the guarded clause product is a mandatory failure control.

The preceding conditional-section task has its raw all-pin existence requirement resolved for the revised source, while its actual graded operator and original-source versions remain open. No claim is made that the old width-eight source lacks such sections.

Checks and verification

The exact GAP control exhausts all 64 nonzero ternary coefficient patterns in two three-coordinate groups and all three targets, with a quintic ten-coordinate control. It verifies 591 affine ranks in mismatched characteristics and 192 failures in matching characteristic. Two groups that merely cover, without one-deletion robustness, give the explicit negative control: four unit coefficients modulo three at target two allow only weight-two tuples and retain a binary parity equation.

Two five-coordinate unit groups modulo three remain covering after three deletions. Across all targets and every at-most-two-bit pin they give 603 conditional affine-full fibres, and all 135 single-quadratic moment ranks are full. The exact decay ratio is \(3^{15}/2^{25}=14348907/33554432<1\). The complete output reaches its success marker in one run, with one harmless GAP global-name warning. These checks validate the rules and scope controls, not the asymptotic good event or a degree lower bound.

Verification gate. The sole fresh-context GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer passed all four claims without mathematical corrections or unused substantive hypotheses. Its optional clarification of the fixed ambient right-inverse matrices is incorporated. It checked the all-pin quantifiers, source/core ledger and unchanged goal assessment; see the review record. The exact all-target subset-sum bound, fourth-moment proof, central-slice law, core-retention lemma and marginal-selector construction were reread with their field and degree restrictions. No outside theorem or framework change is required for this argument.

Process assessment. A local proof-method failure changed the source parameters, with explicit costs and preserved properties, rather than becoming a false exclusion of the old family. The new raw data do not repair the global obstruction by themselves. The sustained lack of near-half goal progress remains for the scheduled architecture review, and the queue rotates without an extra review or more local rank samples.

9 October 2026 — Near-solution supports are too small for a near-half design

Working support-method exclusion; the random and modular families remain unproved hard. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. On near-half-family, return to the Reed–Muller head and test a global reweighting construction for the original random-half-table source. Could weights supported on assignments violating few whole row blocks give a normalized high-degree annihilator? The support and weights may be chosen after the formula is sampled; the test must therefore not assume an independent fixed support.

Route comparison. The complete local ideal sum and larger proper kernels remain candidates. The local-section spell showed why small states and globally frozen coefficient fibres do not supply them. Near-solution reweighting is a distinct global dual proposal: it uses actual full assignments and cancellation in their weights. Before trying to choose those weights, compare the number of available assignments with the necessary design support. This does not replace PC closure by a scalar condition: failure even for a scalar NS design already rejects this support restriction, while success would still leave vector transport open.

New mathematics. The recorded quadratic support bound extends with its input-width cost explicit. An exact binomial first moment then excludes every adaptive design supported on a low-error set, simultaneously over all proof fields. On the random-half source a near-half design cannot be supported on a sublinear number of violated rows, or below any fixed error fraction whose binary entropy is less than one half. The same calculation rules out low-error supports on both central modular sources at their separately counted thresholds.

Goal progress. Unchanged. This rejects a global support-restricted construction, not either formula family. It supplies no PC upper bound, no design supported on the remaining assignments, no proper near-half kernel and no Frege transfer. No formula-specification refinement follows from this method obstruction.

General statement. lem:degree-sensitive-design-support is an all-field, all-width support bound. thm:adaptive-error-support is a finite-parameter probability bound allowing adaptive supports and arbitrary weights. cor:near-solution-design-exclusion applies it at the actual parameters of the random-table and central modular sources.

Pay the degree of the violated input

Let \(D\ge0\) and \(w\ge1\) be integers, and let \(\Gamma\) be polynomials of degree at most \(w\) on a Boolean cube, over any field \(F\). Let a point weight \(\lambda\) have finite nonempty support \(P\), and write \(\Lambda(f)=\sum_{x\in P}\lambda(x)f(x)\). Assume \(\Lambda(1)=1\), every point of \(P\) violates some member of \(\Gamma\), and \(\Lambda(hg)=0\) for every \(g\in\Gamma\) and every polynomial cofactor with ordinary degree \(\deg(hg)\le D\). Boolean axioms may also be present; they vanish on every point and are not the violated inputs used below.

Lemma (degree-sensitive design support). Under these hypotheses, \[|P|\ge2^{\max\{0,D-w+1\}}.\tag{1}\] Global unsatisfiability is sufficient for the support-violation hypothesis but is not necessary.

Proof. Put \(M=|P|\) and \(L=\lfloor\log_2M\rfloor\). Every function on \(P\) is interpolated by a multilinear polynomial of degree at most \(L\). To verify this, take a degree-compatible monomial order on the full vanishing ideal \(I(P)\). Its quotient is \(F^P\), so it has \(M\) standard monomials. Booleanity makes them squarefree, and the standard set is closed under divisors. A standard monomial of degree \(r\) therefore has all \(2^r\) divisors standard, giving \(r\le L\). These standard monomials span all functions on \(P\), proving the interpolation assertion without an extra shattering theorem.

For each \(x\in P\), choose an input \(g_x\) with \(g_x(x)\ne0\) and a degree-at-most-L polynomial \(p_x\) that is its point indicator on \(P\). Then \[H=\sum_{x\in P}g_x(x)^{-1}p_xg_x\tag{2}\] equals one on \(P\), and every summand has ordinary degree at most \(L+w\). If \(D\ge L+w\), annihilation gives \(\Lambda(H)=0\), whereas the pointwise identity gives \(\Lambda(H)=\Lambda(1)=1\). Thus \(D\le L+w-1\), and (1) follows, together with \(M\ge1\). \(\square\)

This is the input-degree extension of the existing design support lemma, using the same interpolation mechanism. It concerns the cardinality of a signed point-weight representation, not the dimension of the truncated kernel or a nonnegative mass. The later failure-set record concerns a different near-refutation object; its warning against inferring design existence from density remains applicable.

Two scope controls are immediate. A point mass at an actual satisfying assignment is a design of every degree, so the support-violation hypothesis cannot be removed. Also take one empty allowed relation on \(w\ge3\) bits, canonically encoded by all width-w point indicators. At \(D=w-1\) no non-Boolean input is active, and a single point mass is a normalized design. Thus the width cost in (1) cannot be silently replaced by the earlier quadratic cost. These are literal all-parameter controls, not numerical extrapolations.

Count the entire adaptive candidate set

Take integer parameters \(v,m\ge1\), \(w\ge1\), \(D\ge0\), and \(0\le r\le m\). Consider a random collection of \(m\) Boolean row relations on \(v\) variables, of widths at most \(w\). Assume that for every fixed full assignment, its row-acceptance indicators are independent Bernoulli variables of a common probability \(p\in(0,1)\). Different full assignments need not have independent outcomes. For a sampled instance let \(Z(x)\) be its number of violated row blocks and \[P_r^+=\{x:1\le Z(x)\le r\},\qquad 0\le r\le m.\tag{3}\] Use the canonical forbidden-tuple inputs of the row system, over any proof field.

Theorem (adaptive error support). The probability that some normalized degree-D NS design over some field has a point-weight representation supported in \(P_r^+\) is at most \[\min\left\{1,\;2^{v-D+w-1}\sum_{j=1}^{r}\binom mj(1-p)^jp^{m-j}\right\}.\tag{4}\] On an unsatisfiable instance the positive-error set equals the set \(Z\le r\), so the same bound controls the joint event of unsatisfiability and such a low-error design. Without the unsatisfiability condition, allowing support on \(Z=0\) adds at most \(2^vp^m\) to the bound.

Proof. For every fixed assignment, \(Z(x)\) is binomial with the stated parameters. Summing point probabilities gives the exact expectation \[\mathbb E|P_r^+|=2^v\sum_{j=1}^{r}\binom mj(1-p)^jp^{m-j}.\tag{5}\] Every point of this set violates an original canonical input. Therefore any supported design, irrespective of its field, adaptive choice of support or weights, would force \(|P_r^+|\ge2^{D-w+1}\) by (1). Markov's inequality gives (4); using a threshold below one only weakens this valid bound when \(D<w-1\). The event of existence over any field is contained in this single cardinality event, so no union over weights or fields is used. Finally expected satisfying assignments are \(2^vp^m\), which bounds the probability that any zero-error point is available. \(\square\)

All probabilities and cardinalities here are ordinary real/integer quantities in the sampling space. No real moment, positivity argument or rank estimate is reduced into characteristic two. The weights in the design remain arbitrary field elements.

Apply the bound to the actual source parameters

Corollary (near-solution design exclusion). For the original independent half-table source with \[k=\lceil2\log_2v\rceil,\quad m=v+k,\quad D=v/2-o(v),\tag{6}\] the joint event of unsatisfiability and a normalized degree-D design supported on at most \(r\) violated row blocks has probability at most \[2^{-D-1}\sum_{j=1}^r\binom mj.\tag{7}\] For \(r=o(v)\) this is \(2^{-v/2+o(v)}\). More generally, for any fixed \(0<\alpha<1/2\) with binary entropy \(H_2(\alpha)<1/2\), and \(r=\lfloor\alpha m\rfloor\), it is at most \[2^{-(1/2-H_2(\alpha))v+o(v)}.\tag{8}\] Thus, with high probability on the source's unsatisfiable good event, every such point-weight representation must reach assignments beyond that linear error threshold. This is not a lower bound on every support point's error count, an average error, or the number of high-error points.

Proof for half tables. Conditional on any scopes, independent tables accept a fixed assignment independently with probability \(p=1/2\), even if scopes overlap or repeat. Put \(w=k\) in (4). The factor is \(2^{v-m-D+k-1}=2^{-D-1}\), proving (7). For \(r\le m/2\), \[\sum_{j=0}^r\binom mj\le2^{mH_2(r/m)}.\tag{9}\] For \(0<r<m/2\), set \(u=r/m\). In the binomial expansion of one, every probability factor \(u^j(1-u)^{m-j}\) with \(j\le r\) is at least \(u^r(1-u)^{m-r}\); divide by this quantity to get (9). The endpoint cases are immediate. If \(r=o(v)\), the entropy tends to zero. If \(r=\lfloor\alpha m\rfloor\), it tends to \(H_2(\alpha)\). Since \(m=v+O(\log v)\), these substitutions prove both asymptotic bounds. The source is unsatisfiable with probability at least \(1-2^{-k}\), so conditioning on that event changes them by at most a factor \((1-2^{-k})^{-1}\). Its other previously proved good properties can be intersected without altering the method's scope. \(\square\)

The same method gives a useful comparison with the central modular sources. For the latest nine-partition source \(v=l2^l,k=16l,m=9v/k,q>v^2\), any fixed \(0<\varepsilon<5/9\) and \(r\le(5/9-\varepsilon)m\) give joint-event probability at most \[2^{-(9\varepsilon/8)v+o(v)}.\tag{10}\] For the retained five-partition source \(k=8l,m=5v/k\), the analogous threshold \(r\le(3/5-\varepsilon)m\), \(0<\varepsilon<3/5\), gives \(2^{-(5\varepsilon/4)v+o(v)}\).

Proof for central rows. For every fixed Boolean assignment, the condition \(\sum_i a_i(x_i-1/2)=0\) is a nonzero linear equation in independent uniform row coefficients, so acceptance probability is \(p=1/q\). Rows have independent coefficient entries even on shared coordinates. From (4), using \(\sum_j\binom mj\le2^m\), \((1-1/q)^j\le1\) and \(j\le r\), the event is bounded by \[2^{v-D+k-1+m}q^{-(m-r)}.\tag{11}\] At the nine-partition parameters, \(m\log_2q>9v/8\), while \(m+k=o(v)\). If \(m-r\ge(4/9+\varepsilon)m\), the negative exponent contributes at least \((1/2+9\varepsilon/8)v\). Since \(v-D=v/2+o(v)\), (10) follows. The same calculation uses \(m\log_2q>5v/4\) and \(m-r\ge(2/5+\varepsilon)m\) for the five-partition source. The bounds are unconditional over coefficient sampling and then intersected with its established good event; no conditioning on nonzero coefficients was inserted into the acceptance law. \(\square\)

What this changes

The proposed support restriction is false even with fully adaptive signed weights. A repair must allow the support to include assignments with many violated rows and obtain cancellation there. Increasing the number of coefficients on the same low-error points, passing to a field extension, or choosing the points after seeing the tables does not evade the cardinality bound. Conversely, including high-error assignments is only necessary; it gives neither an annihilator nor a multiplication-compatible kernel.

The conclusion applies to the original instances and their row inventories. It is not automatically a statement about error counts in an adaptively chosen minimal core, where both the number of rows and the acceptance distribution can change. It is also not a degree upper bound on the original sources. In particular no new structural condition is added to the formula specification from this restricted-method failure.

Follow-up. Continuing the Reed–Muller head. The low-error support proposal is closed in the scopes (7)–(11); the route still permits global cancellation on much larger supports or an independently constructed proper vector kernel. The next cycle is the scheduled architecture review after six research entries. It must compare those genuine remaining mechanisms with the accumulated local constructions and method obstructions, without treating the new support count as goal progress.

Sub-ideas

  • At the scheduled architecture review, identify a concrete mechanism for a normalized global annihilator using assignments with many violated rows, or a materially different proper vector kernel. Require a test of actual cancellation and legal multiplication; support size, local affine fullness and a nonzero unmarked nullspace do not meet that endpoint.

Verification gate. The sole fresh-context GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer passed after integral degree and width parameters were stated explicitly. It checked the adaptive quantifier, ordinary degree costs, satisfying-point exception, entropy bound and both central thresholds, found no unused substantive hypothesis, and agreed with unchanged goal progress. See the review record. The full earlier support lemma, sparse-failure-set distinction, local-design criterion and exact source acceptance laws were reread. The arguments here are analytic: interpolation, the finite binomial expectation and Markov's inequality prove the claims without a numerical parameter sweep. The satisfying-point and inactive-width controls check the essential hypotheses.

Process assessment. This is a scoped development of the recorded support mechanism, not a new claim that generic rank or density proves hardness. Its adaptive quantifier is handled by counting the entire available set once, avoiding an invalid union over possible weights. The near-half implication has remained unchanged through the six-cycle block, so the required review must reassess the architecture rather than extend this construction on promise alone.

9 October 2026 — Topological colour obstructions can have low binary degree

Working degree ceilings and scope controls; scheduled goal-level architecture review. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. Six entries have left the near-half Boolean PC family and its complete Frege transfer open. Which part of the attempted invariant is genuinely necessary, and which proposed alternative reaches a global implication rather than another local property?

New mathematics. An antipodal chain certificate with bounded-read labels compiles into an ordinary characteristic-two Nullstellensatz refutation. For compact fixed-colour graph encodings, vanishing low neighborhood homology therefore gives a constant degree ceiling. A fully counted high-girth critical-graph witness evades this homology screen. Full Kneser graphs have a separate logarithmic-degree parity compilation, without reverse transfer to their edge-minimal cores. Moment and coefficient-grid controls delimit two other proposed constructions.

Goal progress. Unchanged. These are actual upper bounds, a non-vacuous graph-specific restriction and method controls, not a near-half lower bound. The main positive obligation is still to preserve one in an explicit global relation space at the required cutoff and then verify legal multiplication. Complete Frege transfer remains separate.

General statement. thm:parity-chain-degree-ceiling and cor:neighborhood-homology-ceiling compile the precise topological certificate. cor:kneser-parity-ceiling applies a fixed local label map to full graphs only. prop:high-girth-homology-witness proves the graph screen is non-vacuous. prop:perfect-binary-moment-rank and prop:disjoint-product-map-degree give all-parameter scope controls; ex:kernel-review-controls records the exact finite checks.

Across the goal

  • Near-half Boolean PC family. Open. All six research entries since the last goal-level review took this obligation as primary and reported it unchanged. They excluded the old noncentral source, repaired it by central targets, built compatible selectors, proved their dimension and full-module limitations, supplied stronger conditional sections, and excluded low-error point supports. None proved a surviving global unit at the target cutoff. The open-item count has not dropped from two since the review twelve research entries back.
  • Complete Frege transfer. Open. Zero research cycles in this block took this obligation as primary. The imported weighted-map tools apply only after an appropriate old pseudoideal and coherent maps exist. Growing logarithmic width still has no complete transfer ledger. The old family remains the highest-risk prerequisite.

Obstacle

The missing implication is global: an actual unbounded unsatisfiable Boolean source must have a proper kernel containing its active axioms and stable under every legal multiplication after cancellation. Local immunity, all-pin affine fullness, compatible scalar sections, an exponentially large ambient space and a static normalized annihilator do not establish it. The prescribed padded-fall test from the previous review was settled by absorption, but did not control the complete defect space or the unit.

Architecture review

Necessary target. For each fixed relevant \(\ell\ge2\), give a polynomial-size Boolean CNF family on actual \(v\to\infty\), independent of the proposed size exponent, with \(1\notin C_D\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), where \(D=\lfloor v/2-s\rfloor\), \(s=o(v/(\log v)^{\ell-2})\). A proper degree-D linear kernel containing the inputs and closed on its degree-at-most-D-minus-one part suffices. Its exponential quotient dimension and some large free coordinate set are necessary consequences, not optional properties. A separate construction of a larger quotient or a prescribed free set is unnecessary.

Extra requirements. Full Boolean coefficient modules and globally commuting operators add uncharged restriction behavior that the goal does not require. The latest conditional sections are raw data with coefficient degrees as large as the row width; they do not provide degree-one transport. All-pin local surjectivity and a separately chosen common moment vector were sufficient conveniences for that construction, not requirements on every hard formula. A single unit-separating functional for the full row-closed span is a weaker necessary intermediate target; it must not be reported as a PC invariant.

Independent alternative. Before seeing the preferred route, the sole medium reviewer received only the goal and bounded statements. It found no justified new lower-bound architecture and proposed the compact four-colour/Kneser route as an exploratory alternative. It correctly retained the degree and variable budgets and later clarified that the dimension floor is necessary. Its proposed quadratic edge representation is already the proved degree-four translation; it is not new progress. The actual queued Kneser witness uses edge-minimal cores, so full-graph results need not survive deletion. The review below tests a genuinely different implication of topology: a parity certificate can make the original colouring formula easy. The independent-stage response is retained.

Rank normalization. Continue to use one quotient, its actual unit and the induced multiplier maps. Exponential dimension is necessary but does not identify the marked class. A symmetric Gram matrix over a perfect binary field cannot replace positivity, and independent parameter choices do not imply independence of kernels in a shared truncated weight space. The auxiliary imports below distinguish fresh coefficient classes from the full old-variable coefficient module excluded here.

This weakens the next positive deliverable without changing the goal: even a successful static separation leaves multiplication open. Stop refining local conditional ranks as the main task. No automatic exclusion of arbitrary Kneser cores is made.

Put \(K_D=\sum_a(J_a\cap B_{\le D})\), where each \(J_a\) is the cylinder vanishing ideal of its actual row. Finite separation examples do not discharge it. The probability statement concerns the original independent source, not an adaptively selected core.

The existing evaluation duality makes the exact global domain available: if \(E=B_{\le v-D-1}\) and \(U_a\) is the space of functions supported on the allowed cylinder of row \(a\), seek \(w\in\bigcap_a(E+U_a)\) with \(\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^v}w(x)=1\). The identity \(B_{\le D}^{\perp}=E\) under full-cube binary evaluation pairing and the annihilator-of-intersection rule give this description. It is the already known local-design criterion in a Reed–Muller domain, not a new theorem or an assumed solution. A small local coefficient list is not this exponential space. A characteristic-two chain compiler

Let \(K\) be a finite simplicial complex with a simplicial involution \(\tau\). Work with unoriented simplicial chains over \(\mathbb F_2\). Suppose, for an integer \(m\ge1\), fixed chains satisfy \[c_j\in C_j(K;\mathbb F_2),\qquad \operatorname{aug}(c_0)=1,\qquad \partial c_j=(1+\tau)c_{j-1}\quad(1\le j\le m).\tag{1}\] Let \(\Gamma\) be a canonical Boolean CNF. For each vertex \(u\) of \(K\), let a label function \(L_u\) take values in \(\{\pm1,\ldots,\pm m\}\), depend on at most \(b\ge1\) old Boolean bits, and satisfy \(L_{\tau u}=-L_u\) for every assignment. Require a local certification property: if the labels at an edge \(uv\) are opposite, then the assignment violates an original clause whose variables lie in the union of the bits read at \(u,v\). Labels and chains are fixed functions of the source, not choices made after evaluating a proof line.

Theorem (parity chain ceiling). These data give an ordinary Nullstellensatz refutation of \(\Gamma\) through degree at most \(b(m+1)\) over every field of characteristic two. No Boolean reduction is treated as a free inference, and no bound on the number of simplices is required for the degree assertion.

The local parity identity. Call a multiset of labels positively alternating if their absolute values are distinct and, when ordered by absolute value, their signs alternate starting positive; define negatively alternating similarly. Write \(A_j^+(\sigma),A_j^-(\sigma)\) for the zero-one indicators on a j-simplex. For a label multiset with no opposite pair, \[\sum_{\rho\text{ facet of }\sigma}A_{j-1}^+(\rho) =A_j^+(\sigma)+A_j^-(\sigma)\pmod2.\tag{2}\] Here is a complete count. If a label repeats, only deletion of one of a unique repeated pair can make absolute values distinct, and those two contributions agree; otherwise all facets are non-alternating. With distinct absolute values, order the signs. At least two adjacent equal-sign breaks cannot be removed by deleting one entry. Exactly one break gives two alternating facets with the same starting sign. With no break, only deletion of the first or last entry gives an alternating facet, and exactly one starts positive. These cases prove (2), including two-vertex simplices.

Local canonical compilation. Represent each indicator in (2) by its unique multilinear polynomial on the union of the queried bits of that simplex. This union has size at most \(b(j+1)\). Its difference polynomial vanishes on every assignment satisfying the original clauses supported in that union, since each edge then has no opposite labels. For each assignment where the difference is nonzero, choose one violated such clause. The full assignment indicator is exactly that clause's falsity indicator multiplied by the literals on the other coordinates. Expanding the difference in full assignment indicators therefore expresses it as an ordinary linear combination of input multiples, each of degree at most \(b(j+1)\). The cofactor and clause use disjoint variables. Thus (2) is a paid local identity, not a semantic inference with uncharged degree.

Chain summation. Let \(B_j\) be the evaluation of \(A_j^++A_j^-\) on \(c_j\). The just-derived local identities and (1) give \[B_j=\langle A_{j-1}^+,\partial c_j\rangle =\langle A_{j-1}^++A_{j-1}^-,c_{j-1}\rangle=B_{j-1}.\tag{3}\] Antipodality makes the middle equality an exact polynomial identity. Every vertex is alternating with exactly one sign, so \(B_0=\operatorname{aug}(c_0)=1\). A simplex of dimension \(m\) would need \(m+1\) distinct absolute labels to be alternating, so \(B_m=0\). Summing (3) gives an ordinary input-multiple identity for one through degree \(b(m+1)\). All indicator polynomials and their sums are multilinear; equality as Boolean functions is therefore equality as these ordinary polynomials. The construction uses only binary coefficients and works in every characteristic-two extension. \(\square\)

The parity mechanism is the chain form of Fan's alternating-simplex argument; Prescott–Su's constructive theorem and proof were read. The new assertion here is its explicit ordinary-degree compilation for locally readable Boolean labels. No complex or positive-real theorem is reduced into the proof field.

A graph homology screen with constant degree

For a finite simple graph \(G\), let \(N(G)\) be its neighborhood complex: its simplices are vertex sets with a common neighbor. Let \(B_0(G)\) have vertices \((v,+),(v,-)\) and simplices \(A^+\cup B^-\) whenever every vertex of \(A\) is adjacent to every vertex of \(B\). Either side may be empty. Looplessness makes the sides disjoint, and swapping signs is an involution.

Corollary (neighborhood homology ceiling). Let \(G\) have at least one edge, and let \(c\ge2\), \(b=\lceil\log_2c\rceil\). If \[\widetilde H_i(N(G);\mathbb F_2)=0\quad(0\le i\le c-2),\tag{4}\] then its compact b-bit canonical c-colouring CNF has an ordinary characteristic-two Nullstellensatz refutation through degree \(b(c+1)\). For fixed \(c\), the proof and the chain-finding linear algebra have polynomial size in the graph's vertex count. In particular, for four colours, simultaneous vanishing of reduced homology in degrees zero, one and two gives degree at most ten.

Shift the neighborhood homology. Let \(U\) be the union of closed stars of all positive vertices of \(B_0(G)\), and let \(V\) be the full negative simplex. Then \(B_0(G)=U\cup V\), and \(U\cap V\) is exactly the negative copy of \(N(G)\). The space \(U\) is acyclic. To see this without an equivariant homotopy theorem, add the positive stars one at a time. Each star is a cone. Its intersection with the preceding union is also a cone, on the newly added positive vertex: if a face can be extended by that vertex and by some previous positive vertex, it can be extended by both, since positive vertices impose only adjacency to its negative side. These intersections are nonempty. Induction with the simplicial chain exact sequence for a union proves acyclicity. The full simplex \(V\) is acyclic as well.

The same exact sequence gives \(\widetilde H_j(B_0(G);\mathbb F_2)\cong\widetilde H_{j-1}(N(G);\mathbb F_2)\) for \(j\ge1\), and \(B_0(G)\) is connected because the intersection is nonempty. Explicitly, split a cycle into its U and V pieces; their common boundary lies in the intersection, giving the connecting map. Acyclicity of U and V gives its inverse and trivial kernel. Thus (4) makes reduced homology of \(B_0(G)\) vanish through degree \(c-1\).

Choose a single positive vertex as \(c_0\). Its antipodal norm is a reduced zero-cycle, so it bounds \(c_1\). Inductively \((1+\tau)c_{j-1}\) is a cycle since \((1+\tau)^2=0\) in characteristic two, and the homology vanishing fills it by \(c_j\) for \(j\le c\). These are fixed chains (1).

Colour labels and cost. Label \((v,+)\) by the colour of \(v\) and \((v,-)\) by its negative. For invalid b-bit codes, define the label to be colour one; the original domain clauses forbid those codes. Each label reads exactly b bits and is antipodal. Opposite labels on an edge either expose an invalid code or assign the same valid colour to adjacent graph vertices, violating a canonical input within those two bit blocks. Apply the chain theorem with \(m=c\). There are at most \(O(|V(G)|^{j+1})\) j-faces for every fixed \(j\le c\), and each local truth table has at most \(2^{b(c+1)}\) entries. Binary boundary solving and the resulting input-multiple identity therefore have polynomial size when c is fixed. \(\square\)

Consequently a near-half-hard compact four-colour family must eventually fail (4): at least one of these three reduced binary homology groups must be nonzero. This is a condition on that explicit encoding. It does not say that nonzero homology supplies hardness or that every topological invariant yields such a chain certificate.

Full Kneser graphs and the core boundary

Corollary (Kneser parity ceiling). For every \(k\ge1\) and \(n\ge2k+3\), the full graph \(KG(n,k)\), compactly encoded with four colours, has a binary ordinary Nullstellensatz refutation through degree \(4k+6\). This does not upper-bound arbitrary edge-minimal non-four-colourable subgraphs.

Proof. It suffices to use the induced \(KG(2k+3,k)\). Put \(r=2k+3\) and take the order complex of nonempty signed subsets \((A,B)\) of \([r]\), with \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), ordered by inclusion in both coordinates. It is the barycentric subdivision of the boundary of the r-dimensional crosspolytope. Its coordinate hemispheres provide chains (1) through dimension \(m=r-1=2k+2\): in dimension j, sum the full flags in the positive hemisphere on the first \(j+1\) coordinates. Interior facets cancel in pairs, leaving the two hemispheres of the equator. The zero-chain is one positive vertex.

Fix a total order on subsets refining cardinality. If \(|A|+|B|\le2k-2\), give the node absolute label \(|A|+|B|\), with sign determined by which of A and B is larger in that order. Otherwise the larger side contains a k-subset; query the colour of its first k elements, give it absolute label \(2k-2+\text{colour}\), and use that side's sign. This spherical variant of Matoušek's fixed-query labeling is antipodal and uses labels through \(2k+2\), reading at most two old bits at each node.

Along a strict comparable pair, two low labels have different magnitudes, and low and high ranges are disjoint. Opposite high labels query equally coloured disjoint k-sets: if \(A\subseteq A'\), \(B\subseteq B'\), then \(A\cap B'=B\cap A'=\varnothing\). They therefore violate an original Kneser edge clause within the four queried bits. The chain compiler gives degree \(2(m+1)=4k+6\). The labeling and hemisphere arguments are stated completely here; no Frege-to-PC simulation is assumed. \(\square\)

For \(n=2k+4\), the original graph has exponentially many vertices in k, so this is logarithmic in its actual bit count. However, the queued witness selects edge-minimal cores. Deleting edges can remove the inputs used to certify complementary labels and change neighborhood homology. The corollary gives no reverse proof transfer to those cores. The independent review's full-graph suggestion therefore does not settle the candidate that was actually recorded.

The graph screen is non-vacuous

Proposition (high girth witness). There are unbounded edge-minimal non-four-colourable graphs of girth tending to infinity whose compact two-bit CNFs satisfy the accepted structural envelope and have \(\widetilde H_1(N(G);\mathbb F_2)\ne0\). They have width four, polynomial canonical length, essential blocks, at least four block occurrences of every bit, full binary affine row hulls, no common Horn polarity and a locally shattered set of half their bits. No positive-linear or near-half PC lower bound is asserted for this graph witness.

Existence with the actual size counted. Use the classical high-girth probabilistic construction, with the following complete parameters. Fix an integer \(g\ge5\), choose a sufficiently large integer M, and sample a graph with edge probability \(p=M^{-1+1/(2g)}\). Expected cycles of lengths three through \(g-1\) are at most \(g\sqrt M\). Markov's inequality bounds the probability of more than \(M/10\) such cycles by \(10g/\sqrt M\). The expected number of independent sets of size \(\lceil M/5\rceil\) is at most \[2^M\exp\left(-p\binom{\lceil M/5\rceil}{2}\right)=o(1).\tag{5}\] Choose a graph with both properties and delete one vertex from each short cycle. At least \(9M/10\) vertices remain, and no independent set has size \(\lceil M/5\rceil\). A four-colouring would have an independent colour class of size at least \(9M/40>\lceil M/5\rceil\) for large M, a contradiction.

Take an edge-minimal non-four-colourable subgraph and remove isolated vertices. Every remaining vertex has degree at least four; otherwise a four-colouring after deleting that vertex would extend. Its girth is at least g. It is nonbipartite, so its actual vertex count N is at least g. Taking \(g\to\infty\) proves unboundedness even if the core is much smaller than M. There are \(v=2N\) actual Boolean bits, four width-four clauses per edge and length \(O(N^2\log(N+1))\), with no auxiliaries.

Nonzero neighborhood homology. In a graph with no four-cycle, two distinct neighborhoods intersect in at most one vertex. Every neighborhood simplex can be collapsed, fixing its vertices, to a star on those vertices. Explicitly choose a centre and pair every subset S of its other vertices of size at least two with \(S\cup\{\text{centre}\}\), in decreasing order of \(|S|\). At removal time S has that unique coface, and no other neighborhood simplex contains S. These elementary collapses therefore work in the entire complex. The result is a graph on N vertices with \[\sum_v(\deg(v)-1)=2|E(G)|-N\] edges. If it has t connected components, its first binary homology has dimension \(2|E(G)|-2N+t\), which is positive since minimum degree is at least four. This proves the required failure of (4).

Other specification properties. Edge minimality is block minimality, and the unequal-colour relation is essential in every one of its four bits. Each bit occurs in at least four edge blocks, so its branching fraction is one. The twelve allowed four-bit tuples have full binary affine hull, since a nonzero binary affine function cannot vanish on twelve of the sixteen points. After any coordinate polarity, full affine hull means that no coordinate is fixed. If the renamed row were meet-closed, intersecting all its allowed tuples would therefore give its all-zero tuple. A common polarity making every row meet-closed would make the global all-zero assignment satisfy every renamed row, contradicting unsatisfiability. Thus no common Horn polarity exists. Selecting one of the two bits at each vertex gives a locally shattered set of size N: whenever the selected bits agree along an edge, choose the two other bits differently. Thus all earlier structural conditions coexist with the new homology screen. \(\square\)

This replaces neither the general guarded width-five witness nor its proved positive-linear degree. It gives a graph-specific non-vacuity control and trades away Kneser containment while strengthening odd-girth control to full girth. Neither witness supplies the near-half conclusion. The necessary graph-specific homology restriction is adopted only in the compact colouring sub-specification.

Two further scope controls

Proposition (perfect binary moment rank). Let F be a perfect field of characteristic two and B a symmetric bilinear form on a finite-dimensional space. If every vector with \(B(u,u)=0\) lies in the radical of B, then \(\operatorname{rank}B\le1\). In particular a nondegenerate anisotropic symmetric form has dimension at most one.

Proof. In a basis, the cross terms in \(B(u,u)\) cancel and perfectness gives \[B(u,u)=\sum_i b_{ii}u_i^2=\left(\sum_i\sqrt{b_{ii}}u_i\right)^2.\tag{6}\] Its zero set is the kernel of one linear form, or the whole space. The radical is always contained in it. The assumed reverse inclusion therefore makes the radical have codimension at most one. \(\square\)

An actual Boolean moment example over \(\mathbb F_2\) is the sum of point masses at \(01,10,11\). On \(1,x,y\) its moment matrix is \[\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}.\tag{7}\] It has rank three, while x has zero self-pairing and nonzero pairing with y. Thus positivity-style inference from zero norm to a radical vector is invalid. This does not prohibit nondegenerate bilinear pairings, which may be useful without anisotropy, and it does not address imperfect transcendental extensions.

Proposition (product map degree). Let \(g=x_A\), \(h=x_B\) be monomials on disjoint nonempty Boolean variable sets of sizes a,b. Over any field, the minimum possible maximum degree of coefficient polynomials \(u,v\) satisfying both complete accuracy-one companion identities \[g(1-ug-vh)=h(1-ug-vh)=0\tag{8}\] as Boolean functions is \(\min(a,b)\). The minimum has Boolean coefficient images, so fresh Boolean equations do not change it.

Proof. The product \(P=1-ug-vh\) equals one where \(g=h=0\), and (8) makes it zero elsewhere. Hence its unique multilinear representative is \((1-g)(1-h)\), of degree \(a+b\). If both maps have degree at most T, reduction cannot raise \(\deg P\le T+\max(a,b)\), so \(T\ge\min(a,b)\). If \(a\le b\), the maps \(u=1,v=1-g\) attain degree a; exchange the roles otherwise. Both maps are Boolean-valued. This is a costed specialization of the historical independent-input barrier, not a new packing principle. \(\square\)

At \(a=b=2\), fixed old weight one and affine coefficient degree \(T=1\), all \(2^{10}\) binary coefficient pairs fail. The complete block has original joint degree five, so this is a legitimate full-window control at \(D\ge5\) in the old Boolean base. The seven affine coefficient equations reduce to the two three-equation prescriptions forcing u and v each to be one at the all-one old point, plus the contradictory requirement that their sum there be one. Their coefficient and augmented ranks are six and seven. Although seven equation degrees are less than ten parameters, zero solutions remain compatible with finite-field divisibility. Degree-two maps give an explicit repair in their larger paid window. The base is satisfiable and the source is easy with that repair; no hard-family obstruction is claimed.

  • Fan parity and graph topology. Prescott–Su's Fan theorem supplies the alternating-simplex mechanism. The unbounded high-girth witness verifies non-vacuity, not hardness. Test. Passed: the general compilation and the graph-specific consequence are proved, and exact chains and literal unit identities pass. Remaining use must inspect the actual edge-deleted candidate or a new source; no full-graph ceiling is transferred backwards.
  • Positive moment flat extension. The Curto–Fialkow flat-extension theorem, stated on printed page 322, assumes a positive complex moment matrix and constructs a positive atomic representing measure from flat extension. Try to use a moment kernel to control multiplication. Answers. A valid finite-field replacement with a surviving unit and only legal truncated actions could address near-half-pc-family. Test. Falsified for replacing positivity by zero-norm detection over perfect binary fields: (6) forces rank at most one, whereas a proper degree-D kernel requires exponentially many quotient dimensions; (7) is a concrete nondegenerate Boolean moment counterexample. A nonflat graded construction or an isotropic pairing is not excluded.
  • Finite-field zero-count divisibility. Katz's zero-count theorem gives divisibility, not nonemptiness. In the binary degree-sum case this distinction follows directly: if \(\sum_i\deg f_i<r\), summing \(\prod_i(1+f_i)\) over the r-cube gives zero because each monomial misses a coordinate. Answers. A count that genuinely forces a normalized point in a proposed kernel/map parameter space could address the unit-existence gap and later transfer-map choice; ambient dimension or congruence alone cannot. Test. Falsified for that automatic inference by the complete affine coefficient grid above: the degree-sum inequality holds but the grid has zero solutions. Homogenizing without all fresh fields changes the problem, while the full reduced field grid has no point at infinity. The auxiliary raw Ax–Katz count already reduces to ordinary rank-nullity when it can beat the zero-weight fibre; that is not re-registered as new mathematics.

Absurd bridges

  • Quantum error recovery. Knill–Laflamme's recovery criterion controls compressed error products on a complex code space. Translate a marked proof state into a code state and proposed relation errors into correctable operators. Answers. Recovery that also preserved the actual PC kernel under every legal multiplier could answer near-half-pc-family; correctability alone does not identify an error image with zero. Test. Falsified for that identification. On a logical bit tensored with a syndrome bit, let \(P=I_2\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|\) and \(E=I_2\otimes X\). Then \(PEP=0\), \(PE^*EP=P\), and errors in the span of \(I,E\) are exactly recoverable, but \(EP\ne0\) and \(PE^2P=P\). The explicit syndrome recovery is a positive control. These are error operators, not claimed Boolean variable actions; a degree-filtered proof interpretation remains missing.
  • Belief propagation on factor trees. Kschischang–Frey–Loeliger's sum-product rule is exact on cycle-free factor graphs by distributivity, including its semiring formulation. Translate local row states into messages and try to normalize their contraction as a binary witness. Answers. A degree-aware vector-message construction preserving a unit could address near-half-pc-family; exact scalar counting is insufficient. Test. Falsified for automatic normalization: the one-factor tree \(x\ne y\) has messages \((1,1)\) and partition sum two, which is zero over \(\mathbb F_2\). Conditioning \(x=0\) repairs the normalization by selecting the genuine model \(01\), so the failure is not an impossibility theorem for messages. That repair is a satisfiable point witness and does not supply an unsatisfiable truncated invariant; cyclic exactness and degree costs cannot be assumed.

Working retraction criterion and method controls; the global unit remains unresolved. Produced by Codex (gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning).

Question. On near-half-family, develop the constant-cancellation attempt left by the previous entry. Can a row be removed from a putative unit identity by a linear conditional averaging map that does not increase degree, rather than by a chosen point substitution or an ungraded section?

New mathematics. An all-field criterion characterizes every degree-nonincreasing module retraction supported on a Boolean row: the product of its retained coordinates must not reduce to smaller degree on that row. This gives degree-exact deletion when the discarded coordinates are genuinely private. A binary all-parameter control has full conditional affine and single-quadratic moment surjectivity but no such filtered retraction. On the actual random-half source, replacing monomial-order tests by this exact criterion still causes the previously proved whole-context saturation.

Applying it through whole satisfiable contexts is defeated by saturation at the required cutoff. No odd-mass global separator or actual unit decomposition is obtained, and no formula-family upper bound or Frege transfer follows.

General statement. thm:filtered-row-retraction and cor:filtered-row-deletion cover arbitrary Boolean relations over any field. prop:conditional-moment-retraction-gap separates raw conditional ranks from the filtered map. cor:intrinsic-retraction-saturation applies the exact criterion to the original source using the already proved saturation theorem; ex:filtered-retraction-checks records finite rule checks.

Route comparison. Direct lower bounds still need the marked global unit. A private-row retraction could eliminate terms of a constant-valued identity without requiring all degree falls to vanish. This is a concrete method repair to test, not a new structural hardness axiom. The old ENS section-retraction and section-normal-form records supply the deletion mechanism in a special setting with constant private sections; both full proofs were reread. Here an arbitrary supported linear average is allowed and its exact filtration criterion is proved. The new method's failure on full random contexts is recorded immediately rather than refining its local ranks further.

Characterize the filtered module map

Let F be any field, let S and P be disjoint finite Boolean coordinate sets of sizes s and t, and let \(B=F[x_i:i\in S\cup P]/(x_i^2-x_i)\), \(A=F[x_i:i\in S]/(x_i^2-x_i)\). All degrees are those of unique multilinear representatives. Write \(x_T=\prod_{i\in T}x_i\), including \(x_\varnothing=1\), and \(B_{\le-1}=0\). Let \(R\subseteq\{0,1\}^{S\cup P}\), and let \(I(R)\) be its full Boolean vanishing ideal.

Theorem (filtered row retraction). The following are equivalent:

  1. There is an A-linear map \(T:B\to A\) with \(T(1)=1\), \(T(I(R))=0\), and \(\deg T(f)\le\deg f\) for every f.
  2. There is a multilinear \(w\in B\), supported on R, with \(\deg w\le t\), whose coefficient of \(x_P\) is one.
  3. No polynomial of degree at most \(s-1\) agrees with \(x_S\) on R.

Under the second condition the map is \(T(f)=\tau_P(wf)\), where multiplication is in B and \(\tau_P\) takes the coefficient of \(x_P\), leaving a polynomial in A. The map need not be an algebra homomorphism.

Trace pairing and all module maps. In one Boolean coordinate, the pairing taking the coefficient of x in a product has matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) on \(1,x\), of determinant minus one. Tensoring proves that \(\tau_P(uv)\) is a perfect A-bilinear pairing on the free A-module B. Thus every A-linear map has exactly one form \(T(f)=\tau_P(wf)\). Equivalently, at a fixed shared assignment a, \[T(f)(a)=\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}^P}(-1)^{t-|b|}w(a,b)f(a,b).\tag{1}\] The signs are units over every field, including characteristic two. Testing the forbidden point indicators shows that \(T(I(R))=0\) exactly when w is zero off R.

The exact degree condition. Expand \(w=\sum_{Q\subseteq P}w_Q(x_S)x_Q\). For \(M\subseteq P\), Boolean multiplication gives \[T(x_M)=\sum_{Q\supseteq P\setminus M}w_Q.\tag{2}\] If \(\deg w\le t\), each summand on the right has degree at most \(t-|Q|\le|M|\). By A-linearity, multiplying by a shared monomial does not increase the required total degree, so T is filtered. Conversely, if T is filtered, start with \(M=\varnothing\) to see \(\deg w_P\le0\). Descend through subsets Q. In (2) take \(M=P\setminus Q\); all strict-superset coefficients have already been shown to have degree at most \(t-|Q|-1\). Since \(\deg T(x_M)\le|M|=t-|Q|\), it follows that \(\deg w_Q\le t-|Q|\). Hence \(\deg w\le t\). Also \(T(1)=w_P\), so the normalization is precisely \(w_P=1\). This proves equivalence of the first two conditions.

The monic-drop criterion. Let \(k=s+t\), and pair full Boolean functions by \(\tau_{S\cup P}(fg)\). This is nondegenerate by the same tensor calculation. Degree counting and binomial dimension symmetry give \[(B_{\le t})^\perp=B_{\le s-1}.\tag{3}\] The full point basis also gives \(I(R^c)^\perp=I(R)\), because \(I(R^c)\) is the space of functions supported on R and the trace pairing is diagonal on point indicators with nonzero signs. Therefore the annihilator of the allowed weight space is \[(B_{\le t}\cap I(R^c))^\perp=B_{\le s-1}+I(R).\tag{4}\] For \(\deg w\le t\), the pairing \(\tau_{S\cup P}(w x_S)\) is exactly the scalar \(w_P\): a term containing all private coordinates has no room for a positive shared degree. Thus a weight with \(w_P=1\) exists precisely when \(x_S\notin B_{\le s-1}+I(R)\), which is the third condition. A nonzero pairing is scaled to one. Empty coordinate sets and an empty relation are covered by the stated conventions. \(\square\)

The argument is a trace-duality refinement of the recorded local erasure duality, with an explicit marked coefficient and module filtration. It does not rely on positivity or a binary-only averaging convention. Local immunity through s suffices, but is stronger than necessary: the criterion tests only one monic degree drop. Existence implies that the projection of R onto S is the full cube, since otherwise a missing shared assignment indicator would give precisely such a drop.

What row deletion actually permits

Corollary (filtered row deletion). Add other coordinates Z, disjoint from S and P, and arbitrary ideals \(J_b\) in the Boolean algebra C on \(S\cup Z\). Extend all ideals to the Boolean algebra on \(S\cup P\cup Z\). If the theorem's criterion holds for R, then at every integer cutoff \(D\ge0\), \[\left[(I(R)B\cap B_{\le D})+\sum_b(J_bB\cap B_{\le D})\right]\cap C =\sum_b(J_b\cap C_{\le D}).\tag{5}\] Here B in (5) denotes the enlarged Boolean algebra. In particular a unit decomposition through D exists before deleting R if and only if one exists afterwards. This is a statement about these full row-ideal pieces; arbitrary original-generator NS cofactor bounds are not supplied.

Proof. Extend T by the identity on Z. It is C-linear, fixes C, and preserves total degree by the monomial proof above. It kills the extended row ideal I(R). For \(g\in J_bB\), expand in private monomials as \(g=\sum_{M\subseteq P}g_Mx_M\), where each \(g_M\in J_b\); this is the coefficientwise tensor description of an extended ideal. Then \(T(g)=\sum_Mg_MT(x_M)\in J_b\), while the degree does not exceed \(\deg g\). Apply T to a representation of any left-side element to obtain the right-side representation at the same cutoff. The reverse inclusion is immediate. \(\square\)

This extends the earlier constant-section deletion mechanism to all filtered module averages. Its privacy hypothesis is essential to this application: other row ideals must be extended from C. On the original random-half source, every coordinate occurs in at least two row scopes with high probability, so taking P to be genuinely private to one row leaves P empty. For a non-universal R the theorem then rejects deletion: the only A-linear unital map \(B=A\to A\) is the identity. This does not eliminate a row of the full source for free.

Raw conditional moments are insufficient

Proposition (conditional moment gap). Over \(\mathbb F_2\), let \(s\ge3\), \(r\ge3\), take shared variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_s\) and private variables \(u_1,v_1,\ldots,u_r,v_r\), and define the allowed relation by \[x_1\cdots x_s=q(u,v),\qquad q=\sum_{j=1}^r u_jv_j.\tag{6}\] Every full shared assignment has a private fibre with full binary affine hull. On every such fibre, the constant, all private coordinate functions and any one squarefree quadratic in distinct private coordinates are linearly independent. Hence their moment map is onto. Nevertheless there is no filtered retraction fixing the shared Boolean algebra and killing I(R).

Conditional ranks. For the zero fibre of q, zero and all coordinate unit vectors prove full affine hull. For the one fibre, if an affine function vanishes there, fix one pair to \((1,1)\) and vary any coordinate from a different pair, keeping its partner zero and all other coordinates zero. This forces that coordinate's coefficient to vanish. For each coordinate choose a different fixed pair, and then the constant also vanishes. Thus this fibre too is affine-full.

To test an extra monomial ab in two distinct private coordinates, suppose an affine function plus \(c ab\) vanishes on \(q=\epsilon\). If a and b belong to different pairs, set both partners to zero and use a third pair with product epsilon. Vary a and b freely. This is an affine plane in the fibre, and its mixed difference forces c to be zero. If they belong to the same pair, copy a and b into another pair; the two products cancel. Use a third pair with product epsilon and again obtain an affine plane with a,b free. The same difference forces c to be zero. Affine fullness then kills the remaining coefficients. This proves all the claimed moment surjections without averaging by the even fibre sizes.

Filtered obstruction. Equation (6) identifies the retained monomial of degree s with a polynomial of degree two, less than s. It fails the exact criterion. Directly, a filtered retraction would give \(T(q)=x_1\cdots x_s\) while \(\deg T(q)\le2\), a contradiction. Raw point weights for each conditional moment specification exist by the proved ranks, but their dependence on the shared assignment cannot meet the necessary joint filtration. This is a satisfiable local relation, not a near-half formula-family obstruction or an exclusion of the central modular source. \(\square\)

The retraction itself is not required to preserve products. For example, on the three nonzero points of a two-bit cube, the binary weight one has mass one and defines a map to constants with \(T(x)=T(y)=0\) but \(T(xy)=1\). Thus this local averaging theorem does not construct the full Boolean variable action excluded by the earlier coefficient-fibre theorem.

Use the original random-half source with \(k=\lceil2\log_2v\rceil\), \(m=v+k\), and a fixed deterministic context seed of size \(\lfloor v/2-s_v\rfloor\), where \(s_v\ge0\), \(s_v=o(v/\sqrt{k})\). Suppose a monotone whole-context construction absorbs an entire row whenever no filtered retraction for that row can fix its currently retained coordinates \(S=X_a\cap C\). With probability \(1-o(1)\) this exact test grows the context to all v variables in two batches. If all contained rows are then imposed, the resulting context is unsatisfiable. No PC degree upper bound is asserted.

Proof with the existing probability theorem. The full saturation record was reread. On its simultaneous local interpolation event, every row function is represented through degree \(t_0=k-\lfloor k/2-\sqrt k\rfloor-1\). If \(|S|\ge t_0+1\), in particular \(x_S\) agrees on that row with a polynomial of degree at most \(t_0<|S|\). The new exact criterion therefore forbids every filtered retraction, not merely a particular monomial-order reduction. The proposed construction contains the old two-batch process with threshold \(t_0+1\). Its proved fixed-seed saturation and the unconditional good-source intersection give the conclusion. No new independence or adaptive-core claim is needed. \(\square\)

For every fixed \(\ell\ge2\), the specific cutoff deficit used in the current test, \(v/(\log(v+2))^{\ell-1}\), is in this range. Thus exact local retractions do not repair this whole-context architecture at that cutoff. They remain useful for genuinely private eliminations or differently organized coefficient calculations. The actual random family is not excluded. No specification restriction is adopted: the result is a method obstruction, not an upper bound on the family's PC degree.

Question. On near-half-family, test whether row-specific filtered eliminations can be applied term by term in one polynomial identity. New mathematics. The ordinary PC upper bound using local projection shattering strengthens to a field-dependent local filtration condition. A large selected set must admit a filtered retraction in every row separately. The existing guarded width-five family witnesses this stronger condition with unchanged costs and positive linear degree. Its already known guarded product identity now directly refutes automatic assembly of those row-specific retractions into a common linear map.
