Picked. Continuing the user's direction: "We should probably turn the sketch into a theorem before we continue with the goal."

Question. On frege-consequence and the open statement complete Frege transfer: the bounded-depth transfer theorem has free parameters \(K,t_1,\ldots,t_\ell\). For which deficits \(s\), widths and depths does its count exclude polynomial-size refutations?

New mathematics. An explicit lower bound for the ratio of binomial sums in the rate, and with it a corollary: if \(1\notin C_D\) at \(D=\lfloor n/2-s_n\rfloor\) with \((s_n+w_n)(\log n)^{\max\{\ell-2,0\}}=o(n)\), then for every \(A\) and all large \(n\) the formula has no refutation of depth at most \(\ell\) with at most \(n^A\) disjunctions and lines in the system of the theorem. The approximator degrees are polylogarithmic below the top level and \(n^{o(1)}\) at the top.

Goal progress. Advanced on the transfer statement, by a thin step: cor:bounded-depth-size-bound instantiates the preceding theorem and is the first statement that turns its parametrized inequality into a size bound. It is a conditional reduction with a complete proof, from the degree hypothesis of the first open statement, in its free-dimension form with auxiliary affine equations, to a superpolynomial size bound for an explicit depth-\(\ell\) system. Its deficit condition has the same form as the one used in this notebook, with the width paid like the deficit. Unchanged and still required: the equivalence of the system with the goal's \(\mathrm{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege at each depth; and the result remains conditional on Pang's Theorem 4.3.

General statement. lem:binomial-window-ratio holds for all integers \(n,K,\delta\) with \(1\le\delta\), \(2\delta\le K\le n/2\); cor:bounded-depth-size-bound for every fixed number of levels \(\ell\ge1\) and every exponent \(A\).

The ratio

Lemma (binomial window ratio). Let \(N_n(k)=\sum_{j\le k}\binom nj\). For integers \(\delta\ge1\) and \(2\delta\le K\le n/2\), with \(\rho=(K-2\delta+1)/(n-K+2\delta)\),

\[\frac{N_n(K-\delta)}{N_n(K)}\ \ge\ \frac{\rho^{2\delta}}{1+\rho^{2\delta}}\ \ge\ \tfrac12\rho^{2\delta}.\]

If moreover \(K\ge n/2-\sigma\) and \(4\sigma+8\delta\le n/2\), then \(\rho^{2\delta}\ge\exp(-16(\sigma+2\delta)\delta/n)\).

Proof. Put \(b_j=\binom nj\). For \(K-2\delta<j\le K\), \(b_{j-1}/b_j=j/(n-j+1)\ge\rho\), and \(\rho\le1\) since \(K\le n/2\). Hence \(b_{K-\delta-i}\ge\rho^{\delta+i}b_K\ge\rho^{2\delta}b_K\) for \(0\le i\le\delta-1\), the steps from \(K\) down to \(K-\delta-i\) all having \(j>K-2\delta\). So \(N_n(K-\delta)\ge\sum_{i=0}^{\delta-1}b_{K-\delta-i}\ge\delta\rho^{2\delta}b_K\). Also \(N_n(K)=N_n(K-\delta)+\sum_{j=K-\delta+1}^Kb_j\le N_n(K-\delta)+\delta b_K\), as \(b_j\le b_K\) for \(j\le K\le n/2\). Since \(x/(x+\delta b_K)\) increases in \(x\), the ratio is at least \(\delta\rho^{2\delta}b_K/(\delta\rho^{2\delta}b_K+\delta b_K)\), and \(\rho^{2\delta}\le1\) gives the second inequality. For the last statement, \(1-\rho=(n-2K+4\delta-1)/(n-K+2\delta)\le(2\sigma+4\delta)/(n/2)\), so \(\rho\ge1-x\) with \(x=(4\sigma+8\delta)/n\le\tfrac12\), and \(1-x\ge e^{-2x}\) on \([0,\tfrac12]\). \(\square\)

The size bound

Corollary (bounded depth size bound). Fix \(\ell\ge1\) and \(A>0\). For each \(n\) in an infinite set let \(F_n\) be a CNF of width \(w_n\) and \(\Lambda_n\) a set of affine equations over \(\mathbb F_2\) with free dimension \(n\), and suppose \(1\notin C_D\) for the closure of the transfer theorem at \(D=\lfloor n/2-s_n\rfloor\), \(s_n\ge0\), with

\[(s_n+w_n)(\log n)^{\max\{\ell-2,0\}}=o(n).\]

Then for all large \(n\), \(F_n\) has no refutation of depth at most \(\ell\) in the system of the transfer theorem in which the number of distinct disjunctions plus the number of distinct lines is at most \(n^A\). The statement is conditional on Pang's Theorem 4.3, as the transfer theorem is.

Proof. Write \(e=\max\{\ell-2,0\}\), \(\sigma^*=s_n+w_n+4\sqrt n+2\) and \(K=\lfloor n/2-\sigma^*\rfloor\), so \(n/2-K\le\sigma^*+1=:\sigma\) and \(\sigma(\log n)^e=o(n)\). Put \(\Theta=\ln(\ell n^A)\) and \(c=8A+1\). With \(K\) fixed, define inductively \(\Delta_0=1\), \(\eta_i=\eta_K(\Delta_{i-1})\), \(t_i=\lceil\Theta/\eta_i\rceil+1\), \(\Delta_i=\Delta_{i-1}t_i\); the induction below shows \(\Delta_{i-1}\le K\) for large \(n\), so each \(\eta_i\) is positive and the definition makes sense. By the lemma, whenever \(2\Delta_{i-1}\le K\) and \(4\sigma+8\Delta_{i-1}\le n/2\),

\[\eta_i\ \ge\ \tfrac14\exp\bigl(-16(\sigma+2\Delta_{i-1})\Delta_{i-1}/n\bigr).\]

Levels below the top (none if \(\ell=1\)). Take \(n\) large enough that \(c\log n\ge1\). By induction \(\Delta_i\le(c\log n)^i\) for \(i\le\ell-1\) and large \(n\): if \(\Delta_{i-1}\le(c\log n)^{i-1}\le(c\log n)^{e}\) (for \(\ell\ge2\), \(i-1\le\ell-2\)), the exponent is at most \(16(\sigma+2(c\log n)^e)(c\log n)^e/n\to0\), so \(\eta_i\ge\tfrac18\) and \(t_i\le8\Theta+2\le c\log n\) for large \(n\).

Top level. \(\Delta_{\ell-1}\le(c\log n)^{\ell-1}\), and the exponent is at most \(16c^{\ell-1}(\log n)\cdot(\sigma+2(c\log n)^{\ell-1})(\log n)^{e}/n\) when \(\ell\ge2\), which is \(o(\log n)\); when \(\ell=1\) it is \(16(\sigma+2)/n\to0\). So \(\eta_\ell\ge n^{-o(1)}\), \(t_\ell\le n^{o(1)}\) and \(\Delta=\Delta_\ell\le n^{o(1)}\le\sqrt n\) for large \(n\).

The hypotheses of the transfer theorem: \(\Delta\le K\le n\) and the side conditions of the lemma hold for large \(n\); and \(K+\max\{4\Delta,\Delta+w_n\}\le n/2-\sigma^*+4\sqrt n+w_n=n/2-s_n-2\le D\). For a refutation with \(\sum_iS_i\le n^A\), \(\sum_iS_i(1-\eta_i)^{t_i}\le\sum_iS_ie^{-\eta_it_i}\le n^Ae^{-\Theta}\max_ie^{-\eta_i}<1/\ell\le1\), contradicting the theorem. \(\square\)

Reading. The number of levels \(\ell\) counts the line itself: \(\ell=1\) is lines of literals and parities of literals with cut, where a deficit and width \(o(n)\) suffice; \(\ell=2\) allows one layer of disjunctions inside lines and also needs only \(o(n)\); each further layer costs a factor \(\log n\) in the deficit this proof can admit, which is a sufficient condition and not shown necessary. The condition has the same form as \(s=o(v/(\log v)^{\ell-2})\) in the open statements, here in the free dimension \(n\) and with the width \(w_n\) in the same budget; how \(\ell\) levels correspond to a standard depth is open. Affine equations need not belong to the formula and do not count. The bound is in terms of \(n\); in terms of formula length it is superpolynomial when the length is polynomial in \(n\).

Not covered. The comparison with a standard definition of \(\mathrm{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege, including which standard depth corresponds to \(\ell\) levels; any quantitative bound beyond "not polynomial"; fields other than \(\mathbb F_2\).

9 October 2026 — Bounded-depth Frege with parity connectives is simulated by the transfer theorem's system with a constant number of extra levels

Working proof of the simulation for Krajíček's \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\); with it the size bound holds for that system, conditional on Pang's Theorem 4.3. User-picked, out of queue order. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Picked. Continuing the user's direction: "We should probably turn the sketch into a theorem before we continue with the goal."

Question. On frege-consequence and the open statement complete Frege transfer: the size bound is for a one-sided sequent system. Does it hold for a standard bounded-depth Frege system with parity connectives, and with how many levels for depth \(d\)?

New mathematics. For the system \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\) as defined by Krajíček, every refutation of a CNF with \(S\) symbols translates into a refutation in the sequent system, with parity taken over multisets, having at most \(d+c_F\) levels and \(O_F(S^3)\) disjunctions and lines, \(c_F\) depending only on the underlying Frege system. Hence the size bound holds for \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\) with \(\ell=d+c_F\).

Goal progress. Advanced on the transfer statement: cor:frege-parity-size-bound is the statement the open item asks for, for a source-defined \(\mathrm{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege system at every fixed depth, as a conditional reduction with a complete proof: a degree barrier at \(\lfloor n/2-s\rfloor\) in the free dimension, with \(s+w\) below \(n/(\log n)^{d+c_F-2}\) in order, excludes polynomial-size depth-\(d\) refutations. What remains of the transfer statement is its condition, Pang's Theorem 4.3, an imported result of a first arXiv version that has had one reading here; and the proofs of the last three entries have had one reviewer each.

General statement. prop:frege-parity-simulation holds for every Frege system in the DeMorgan language, every depth and every CNF; cor:frege-parity-size-bound for every fixed depth and exponent; lem:small-line-completeness for all finite sets of formulas taken as atoms.

The source system

From Krajíček, arXiv:2301.10617v3, Section 5, read in this cycle. \(F\) is any Frege system in the language \(0,1,\neg,\vee,\wedge\): finitely many sound schematic rules, implicationally complete. \(F(\mathrm{MOD}_p)\) adds connectives \(\mathrm{MOD}_{p,i}\) of unbounded arity, true when the number of true arguments is \(i\) modulo \(p\), accepts all rules of \(F\) for all formulas of the extended language, and adds the axioms \(\mathrm{MOD}_{p,0}(\emptyset)\), \(\neg\mathrm{MOD}_{p,i}(\emptyset)\) for \(i\ne0\), and \(\mathrm{MOD}_{p,i}(\Gamma,\varphi)\equiv[(\mathrm{MOD}_{p,i}(\Gamma)\wedge\neg\varphi)\vee(\mathrm{MOD}_{p,i-1}(\Gamma)\wedge\varphi)]\). Depth: constants and atoms have depth \(0\); negation and each \(\mathrm{MOD}\) add one; a formula formed by repeated \(\vee\) from formulas none of which starts with \(\vee\) has depth one more than their maximum, and likewise for \(\wedge\). \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_p)\) uses formulas of depth at most \(d\). The source does not spell out refutations of a CNF; I take: a sequence of formulas of depth at most \(d\), each a clause of the CNF written as a disjunction of literals, an instance of a rule of \(F\) or a \(\mathrm{MOD}\) axiom, ending with \(0\); its size \(S\) is its number of symbols. I take \(\equiv\) as the conjunction of the two implications written with \(\neg,\vee\). Here \(p=2\).

The target system, with multiset parity

The system of the bounded-depth transfer theorem, with one change: \(\bigoplus\) is applied to finite multisets of formulas, the value of \(\bigoplus M\) is the sum of the values with multiplicity, and the parity axioms are stated for \(M=M'+A\), \(M\) being \(M'\) with one more copy of \(A\). The theorem and its corollary hold for this system with the same proofs: the proofs use of parity only that \(V_{\bigoplus M}=V_{\bigoplus M'}+V_A\) identically and that parity adds no level. This variant is what is used below; the set version is the special case.

Tools in the target system

Call a formula or line schematic over formulas \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) if it is built from them, as atoms, by \(\neg\) and disjunctions of sets, the built part having at most \(c\) symbols.

Lemma (small line completeness). Let \(L,L_1,\ldots,L_k\) be lines schematic over \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\). If every assignment of truth values to the atoms that satisfies every \(L_i\), under the reading of \(\neg\), disjunction and lines as disjunctions, satisfies \(L\), then \(L\) is derivable from \(L_1,\ldots,L_k\) by a derivation whose number of lines is bounded in terms of \(m,c,k\), all of whose members are schematic over the atoms with at most \(c\) symbols, hence of level at most \(c\) above the atoms' levels.

Proof. Decomposition: from \(\Gamma\cup\{\bigvee T\}\) derive \(\Gamma\cup T\), by cutting with \(\{\neg\bigvee T\}\cup T\), which follows by the negated-disjunction rule from the lines \(\{\neg A\}\cup T\), \(A\in T\), each a weakening of an identity; from \(\Gamma\cup\{\neg\bigvee T\}\) derive \(\Gamma\cup\{\neg A\}\) for \(A\in T\), by cutting with \(\{\bigvee T,\neg A\}\), obtained from an identity by the disjunction rule; from \(\Gamma\cup\{\neg\neg A\}\) derive \(\Gamma\cup\{A\}\) by the converse double-negation rule. Cuts are applied after weakening both premises to a common context. Following the schematic structure, each \(L_i\) is decomposed into finitely many lines whose members are atoms or negated atoms, jointly equivalent to \(L_i\). In the same way \(L\) is equivalent to a set of such clauses, from which it is recomposed by the disjunction, negated-disjunction and double-negation rules. Each of these clauses is a propositional consequence of the clauses of the \(L_i\); cut and weakening on clauses over atoms are resolution with weakening, which is implicationally complete; a clause containing an atom and its negation is a weakening of an identity. Recomposition also uses weakening, for instance to add an empty disjunction. The derivation is made with formally distinct atoms and the formulas \(X_j\) are substituted afterwards: every rule of the target system is closed under substitution, lines being sets and no flattening taking place, so atoms that coincide or are syntactically related cause no difficulty. \(\square\)

Flattening. For sets \(T,U\) of formulas the lines \(\{\neg\bigvee(T\cup\{\bigvee U\}),\bigvee(T\cup U)\}\) and \(\{\neg\bigvee(T\cup U),\bigvee(T\cup\{\bigvee U\})\}\) have derivations with \(O(|T|+|U|)\) lines: for the first, by the negated-disjunction rule from \(\{\neg X,\bigvee(T\cup U)\}\), \(X\in T\), each from an identity by the disjunction rule, and \(\{\neg\bigvee U,\bigvee(T\cup U)\}\), itself by the negated-disjunction rule from the lines \(\{\neg A,\bigvee(T\cup U)\}\), \(A\in U\); for the second, from \(\{\neg X,\bigvee(T\cup\{\bigvee U\})\}\) for \(X\in T\), and for \(X\in U\) by two uses of the disjunction rule from an identity. The same holds with \(\neg\neg\bigvee U\) in place of \(\bigvee U\), using the double-negation rule.

Congruence. From \(\{\neg A,B\}\) and \(\{\neg B,A\}\): \(\{\neg\neg A,\neg B\}\) and \(\{\neg\neg B,\neg A\}\) by double negation; \(\{\neg\bigvee(T\cup\{A\}),\bigvee(T\cup\{B\})\}\) and its converse by the negated-disjunction and disjunction rules as above, in \(O(|T|)\) lines; and \(\{\neg\bigoplus(M+A),\bigoplus(M+B)\}\) and its converse, by the lemma applied to the atoms \(\bigoplus(M+A),\bigoplus(M+B),\bigoplus M,A,B\) and the eight parity axiom lines for \(M+A\) and \(M+B\), of which the wanted lines are propositional consequences together with the two given lines. The parity case is not needed below: the schemas of \(F\) contain no \(\mathrm{MOD}\), and the \(\mathrm{MOD}\) axiom is treated with its \(\mathrm{MOD}\) formulas as atoms.

The translation

For a formula \(\varphi\) of the source language define \(\varphi^*\): \(x^*=x\); \(0^*=\bigvee\emptyset\), \(1^*=\neg\bigvee\emptyset\); \((\neg\varphi)^*=\neg\varphi^*\); for a maximal \(\vee\)-block with members \(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_k\), none starting with \(\vee\), \(\bigvee\{\varphi_i^*\}\); for a maximal \(\wedge\)-block, \(\neg\bigvee\{\neg\varphi_i^*\}\); \(\mathrm{MOD}_{2,1}(\Gamma)^*=\bigoplus\Gamma^*\) and \(\mathrm{MOD}_{2,0}(\Gamma)^*=\neg\bigoplus\Gamma^*\), \(\Gamma^*\) the multiset of translations. Values are preserved. Each block becomes one disjunction and negation and parity add no level, while a constant becomes an empty disjunction; so the level of \(\varphi^*\) is at most the depth of \(\varphi\) plus one. The source's depth also counts negations and \(\mathrm{MOD}\), which the level ignores, so the translation covers the more generous measure of nesting of blocks.

Proposition (Frege parity simulation). For every Frege system \(F\) there is a constant \(c_F\) such that every \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\)-refutation with \(S\) symbols of a CNF translates into a refutation of the same CNF in the target system with at most \(d+c_F\) levels, in which the number of distinct disjunctions plus distinct lines is at most \(c_FS^3\).

Proof. We derive the line \(\{\varphi^*\}\) for every formula \(\varphi\) of the refutation, in order.

Schematic and flattened translations. Let \(A(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\) be a formula of the source language of constant size, a schema, and \(\sigma\) a substitution. Let \(A^\circ\) be the translation of \(A\) with the \(p_j\) as atoms, followed by replacing \(p_j\) by \(\sigma(p_j)^*\); it is schematic over the \(\sigma(p_j)^*\), and over the parity formulas occurring in it when \(A\) contains \(\mathrm{MOD}\). It differs from \((\sigma A)^*\) only where a block of \(A\) has a member \(p_j\) and \(\sigma(p_j)\) starts with the block's connective, so that the blocks merge in \((\sigma A)^*\); for a \(\wedge\)-block the member appears in \(A^\circ\) as a doubly negated disjunction. By induction on \(A\), the lines \(\{\neg(\sigma A)^*,A^\circ\}\) and \(\{\neg A^\circ,(\sigma A)^*\}\) are derivable: at a block, apply flattening once for each merging member, in its plain form for \(\vee\)-blocks and its double-negation form for \(\wedge\)-blocks, and congruence for the subformulas already treated; at a negation, congruence; the equivalences are chained by weakening and cut. The number of flattening and congruence steps is bounded in terms of \(A\), and each takes a number of lines linear in the number of members of the disjunctions involved, which is at most \(S\).

Rules of \(F\). Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_k/A_0\) be a rule and \(\sigma\) the substitution of an instance whose premises have been derived as \(\{(\sigma A_i)^*\}\). Cutting with the lines above gives \(\{A_i^\circ\}\). The rule is sound, so the line \(\{\neg A_1^\circ,\ldots,\neg A_k^\circ,A_0^\circ\}\) is schematic over the \(\sigma(p_j)^*\) and true under every assignment to them; by the lemma it is derivable in a number of lines depending only on the rule. Constants in the rule are empty disjunctions and their negations, which are schematic and have the right truth values. Cuts give \(\{A_0^\circ\}\), and a cut with \(\{\neg A_0^\circ,(\sigma A_0)^*\}\) gives \(\{(\sigma A_0)^*\}\).

Parity axioms. \(\mathrm{MOD}_{2,0}(\emptyset)\) and \(\neg\mathrm{MOD}_{2,1}(\emptyset)\) both translate to \(\neg\bigoplus\emptyset\), an axiom line. The third axiom, for \(i=0,1\), is an instance of a constant-size schema in the atoms \(\mathrm{MOD}_{2,i}(\Gamma,\varphi)\), \(\mathrm{MOD}_{2,i}(\Gamma)\), \(\mathrm{MOD}_{2,i-1}(\Gamma)\), \(\varphi\); its schematic translation is schematic over \(\bigoplus(\Gamma^*+\varphi^*)\), \(\bigoplus\Gamma^*\), \(\varphi^*\) and is a propositional consequence of the four parity axiom lines for \(\Gamma^*+\varphi^*\); the lemma derives it, and the flattened form follows as for rules.

Clauses and the end. A clause of the CNF with literals \(l_1,\ldots,l_k\), \(k\ge2\), translates to \(\bigvee\{l_i\}\), derived from the initial line \(\{l_1,\ldots,l_k\}\) by \(k\) uses of the disjunction rule; for \(k=1\) the initial line is the translation. The last formula \(0\) gives the line \(\{\bigvee\emptyset\}\); the line \(\{\neg\bigvee\emptyset\}\) follows by the negated-disjunction rule with no premises, and a cut gives the empty line.

Levels and size. Every member of every line is \(\varphi^*\) for a subformula \(\varphi\) of the refutation, or schematic with boundedly many symbols over such formulas and parities of them. So disjunctions have level at most \(d+c\) and lines at most \(d+c+1\), with \(c\) bounded by the sizes of the schemas of \(F\) and of the parity axiom, plus one for constants. Each of at most \(S\) steps uses \(O_F(S)\) lines, each with \(O_F(1)\) members of \(O_F(S)\) symbols, except the lines for clauses, which have up to \(S\) members that are literals and one disjunction; so there are \(O_F(S^2)\) lines and \(O_F(S^3)\) distinct disjunctions. \(\square\)

Corollary (Frege parity size bound). Fix a Frege system \(F\), a depth \(d\ge1\) and \(A>0\), and put \(\ell=d+c_F\). Let \(F_n\), \(\Lambda_n\), \(w_n\), \(s_n\) be as in the bounded depth size bound, with \(1\notin C_D\) at \(D=\lfloor n/2-s_n\rfloor\) and \((s_n+w_n)(\log n)^{\ell-2}=o(n)\). Then for all large \(n\), \(F_n\) has no \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\)-refutation with at most \(n^A\) symbols. In particular a single family with \(s_n+w_n\le n^{1-\epsilon}\) for some fixed \(\epsilon>0\) has no polynomial-size refutation at any fixed depth. Conditional on Pang's Theorem 4.3.

Proof. A refutation with \(S\le n^A\) symbols gives, by the proposition, a refutation with at most \(\ell\) levels and at most \(c_Fn^{3A}\le n^{3A+1}\) disjunctions and lines, excluded by the size bound, in its multiset form, with exponent \(3A+1\). \(\square\)

Scope

The constant \(c_F\) is not computed. Only soundness and finiteness of the rules of \(F\) are used, not its completeness. The source refutation uses the clauses only: the affine equations \(\Lambda\) are not premises of the proof, in either system; they enter the degree hypothesis alone. Size is the number of symbols, not of lines. The corollary's size is in symbols and in terms of the free dimension \(n\); for a formula of length polynomial in \(n\) it is superpolynomial in the length. The refutation format and the reading of \(\equiv\) are my reading of the source where it is silent. Only \(p=2\) is treated. Sequent formulations of the source systems are not treated; the source states that they agree with Frege formulations up to an additive constant in depth, which is not checked here.

Specification decision. No change beyond the preceding entry's: the deficit and the width share the budget \(o(n/(\log n)^{d+c_F-2})\) at depth \(d\), and a family meant for all depths should aim at a polynomially small deficit ratio, \(s_n+w_n\le n^{1-\epsilon}\). That is a stronger target than each fixed depth needs and is recorded as a target, not as a requirement.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer, with the source's text and the two preceding entries, found no error that breaks the proposition or the corollary. It confirmed the restatement of the source system, that the transfer proof is unchanged for multiset parity, the three decomposition derivations, flattening and congruence rule by rule, the \(\mathrm{MOD}\) axioms at \(p=2\), the clause and final lines, and the corollary's exponent. One claim was false as written, that the level of a translation is at most the source depth: constants add one, now stated and absorbed in \(c_F\). Other corrections applied: atoms that coincide are handled by substitution after deriving with distinct atoms; weakening in recomposition; a non-difference removed from the comparison of the two translations; the size count for clause lines; three scope items. Unused and now marked: completeness of \(F\), and the parity case of congruence. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing. The check asked which constraints the transfer places on the family and on the auxiliary equations. With this entry the answer is a proved statement: a literal CNF of free dimension \(n\) with a degree barrier at \(\lfloor n/2-s\rfloor\), deficit and width in the stated budget, auxiliary affine equations allowed outside the formula. Its queued sub-ideas remain open, first among them an independent check of the imported theorem, so the item is not developed; the next attempt on it is that check.

9 October 2026 — The imported theorem proved in full at characteristic two: the transfer no longer rests on a citation

Working proofs, following Pang's Sections 3 and 4 at \(p=2\) with the free dimension; with them the Frege transfer is a working proof without imported premises. User-picked, out of queue order. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Picked. Continuing the user's direction: "We should probably turn the sketch into a theorem before we continue with the goal. It rests on the assumption that Pang was right".

Question. On frege-consequence and the open statement complete Frege transfer: the last three entries are conditional on the first part of Theorem 4.3 of Pang's paper. Can that statement, at \(p=2\) and with the free dimension, be proved here in full, so that the transfer depends on no unreviewed source?

New mathematics. No new idea: the proof is Pang's, specialized to \(\mathbb F_2\) and written out with every degree condition, in four steps: rank under specialization, descent of a kernel stable under squaring, the application to multiplication maps, and the monotone normalized rank with its gain. The free dimension enters in one place. With this the transfer for \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\) is stated as one theorem without conditions.

Goal progress. Advanced on the transfer statement: thm:near-half-frege-transfer is now a working proof whose every step is recorded in this notebook, in four entries. The second open statement is thereby discharged within the simulation entry's limits: for \(p=2\), for the Frege and not the sequent formulation of \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\), with \(c_F\) not computed, and with size counted in symbols as a function of \(n\), hence superpolynomial in formula length only when the length is polynomial in \(n\); and subject to the usual status of working proofs. The first open statement, the family, is untouched.

General statement. thm:binary-approximator-rank holds for every polynomial set over \(\mathbb F_2\) containing the Boolean axioms and all parameters with \(1\le d\le K\le n\), \(dt+K+d\le D\); thm:near-half-frege-transfer for every Frege system, depth and exponent.

Setting

\(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_v]\) contains the Boolean axioms \(x_i^2+x_i\). \(C_D\) is the set of polynomials derivable from \(\mathcal Q\) by polynomial calculus within degree \(D\): the closure of the elements of \(\mathcal Q\) of degree at most \(D\) under sums and under multiplication of elements of degree at most \(D-1\) by a variable. \(V_k\) is the space of polynomials of degree at most \(k\). Two standard facts. (M) If \(g\in C_D\) and \(\deg g+\deg u\le D\), then \(gu\in C_D\): multiply by the variables of each monomial of \(u\) one at a time. (B) For \(g\) of degree at most \(e\le D/2\), \(g^2+g\in C_D\): it vanishes on the cube and has degree at most \(2e\), and a polynomial of degree at most \(D\) vanishing on the cube is a combination of multiples \(m\,(x_i^2+x_i)\) of degree at most its own. For a field \(E\supseteq\mathbb F_2\) put \(C_D^E=E\otimes C_D\subseteq E[x]_{\le D}\); then \(C_D^E\cap E[x]_{\le j}=E\otimes(C_D\cap V_j)\), since extension of scalars commutes with intersections of subspaces, and hence (M) holds over \(E\): if \(G\in C_D^E\), \(u\in E[x]\) and \(\deg G+\deg u\le D\), then \(Gu\in C_D^E\).

Fix a set of affine elements of \(\mathcal Q\), possibly empty, consistent as a linear system, and let \(\varrho\) be the rank of their linear parts; put \(n=v-\varrho\), \(v\) the number of variables of the ring. \(N_n(k)=\sum_{j\le k}\binom nj\).

Rank retention

Lemma (binary rank retention). Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_s\) have degree at most \(a\), \(h_1,\ldots,h_r\) degree at most \(b\), and \(b+k+2a\le D\). Let \(M_i:V_k\to(V_D/C_D)^r\), \(M_if=([fg_ih_j])_j\), and \(\overline M=(M_1,\ldots,M_s)\) the stacked map. Then some \(c\in\mathbb F_2^s\) has \(\operatorname{rank}\sum_ic_iM_i\ge\tfrac12\operatorname{rank}\overline M\).

Proof. Step 1, multiplicities. For a nonzero polynomial \(H\) in \(s\) variables over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(e\in\mathbb F_2^s\) let \(\operatorname{mult}(H,e)\) be the least degree of a term of \(H(e+z)\). Then \(\sum_e\operatorname{mult}(H,e)\le\deg H\cdot2^{s-1}\). For \(s=1\) this is the count of roots with multiplicity. For \(s>1\) write \(H(y,z)=\sum_{j\le t}H_j(y)z^j\), \(H_t\ne0\). Fix \(e'\in\mathbb F_2^{s-1}\), let \(\mu=\operatorname{mult}(H_t,e')\) and \(y^\alpha\) a monomial of degree \(\mu\) in \(H_t(e'+y)\). The coefficient \(h_\alpha(z)\) of \(y^\alpha\) in \(H(e'+y,z)\) has degree exactly \(t\). For \(e_s\in\mathbb F_2\), \(H(e'+y,e_s+z)\) contains \(y^\alpha\) times the lowest term of \(h_\alpha(e_s+z)\), and different monomials in \(y\) do not cancel, so \(\operatorname{mult}(H,(e',e_s))\le\mu+\operatorname{mult}(h_\alpha,e_s)\). Summing over \(e_s\) gives at most \(2\mu+t\); summing over \(e'\) and using induction for \(H_t\) gives at most \(2\deg H_t\,2^{s-2}+t2^{s-1}\le\deg H\cdot2^{s-1}\).

Step 2, specialization. Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_s\) be matrices over \(\mathbb F_2\) of one shape, \(A(\lambda)=\sum\lambda_iA_i\) with indeterminates \(\lambda_i\), and \(R\) its rank over \(E=\mathbb F_2(\lambda)\). Then the average of \(\operatorname{rank}A(e)\) over \(e\in\mathbb F_2^s\) is at least \(R/2\). If \(R>0\), take an \(R\times R\) submatrix \(B(\lambda)\) with \(H=\det B\ne0\), of degree at most \(R\). For \(e\) let \(\rho_e\le\operatorname{rank}A(e)\) be the rank of \(B(e)\). Row operations over \(\mathbb F_2\) make \(R-\rho_e\) rows of \(B(e)\) vanish without changing the determinant; as \(B(e+z)=B(e)+B(z)\), those rows of \(B(e+z)\) are linear forms in \(z\), so every term of \(H(e+z)\) has degree at least \(R-\rho_e\). Thus \(R-\operatorname{rank}A(e)\le\operatorname{mult}(H,e)\), and Step 1 gives the average.

Step 3, descent. Let \(W\subseteq E^m\) be an \(E\)-subspace, \(E\) of characteristic two, closed under squaring of all coordinates. Then \(W\) has a basis in \(\mathbb F_2^m\): if \(T\) is the reduced row echelon basis matrix of \(W\), the matrix of squares of its entries has rows in \(W\), the same pivots and the same echelon form, so its rows are independent elements of \(W\), as many as its dimension, and it is a reduced echelon basis matrix of \(W\); it equals \(T\) by uniqueness, and the entries of \(T\) satisfy \(c^2=c\).

Step 4, kernels. Let \(A_i:U\to W'\) be linear maps of finite-dimensional \(\mathbb F_2\)-spaces, in matrix form. The entries of \(A(\lambda^2)=\sum\lambda_i^2A_i\) are the squares of those of \(A(\lambda)\), so its minors are the squares of the minors and the ranks over \(E\) agree. Suppose \(\ker_EA(\lambda)\subseteq\ker_EA(\lambda^2)\). Then the kernels are equal. For \(u\in\ker_EA(\lambda)\), squaring the coordinates of \(A(\lambda)u=0\) gives \(A(\lambda^2)u^{[2]}=0\), so the kernel is closed under squaring of coordinates and has a basis in \(U\) by Step 3. For \(u\in U\), \(\sum\lambda_iA_iu=0\) forces every \(A_iu=0\), the \(\lambda_i\) being independent over \(\mathbb F_2\). So \(\ker_EA(\lambda)=E\otimes\bigcap_i\ker A_i\) and \(\operatorname{rank}_EA(\lambda)=\operatorname{rank}\overline A\).

Step 5, multiplication maps. Extend the \(M_i\) over \(E\); \(E\otimes(V_D/C_D)=E[x]_{\le D}/C_D^E\). Let \(f\in\ker_EM(\lambda)\), so with \(q_\lambda=\sum\lambda_ig_i\), \(h_jq_\lambda f\in C_D^E\) for all \(j\), of degree at most \(b+a+k\). Multiplying by \(q_\lambda\), of degree at most \(a\), \(h_jq_\lambda^2f\in C_D^E\) by (M) over \(E\), as \(b+k+2a\le D\). Now \(q_\lambda^2=\sum\lambda_i^2g_i^2\), and \(h_j(g_i^2+g_i)f\in C_D^E\) by (B) and (M) over \(E\), degree \(2a+b+k\le D\). Hence \(\sum\lambda_i^2h_jg_if\in C_D^E\), that is \(f\in\ker_EM(\lambda^2)\). By Step 4 the rank of \(M(\lambda)\) over \(E\) is \(\operatorname{rank}\overline M\), and by Step 2 some specialization has rank at least half of it. \(\square\)

Normalized rank and gain

Fix \(g_1,\ldots,g_s\) of degree at most \(d\ge1\) and \(P\in V_a\). For \(k\) with \(a+k+d\le D\) let \(Z_P(k)=\{f\in V_k:Pg_if\in C_D\text{ for all }i\}\) and \(c_P(k)=\dim V_k/Z_P(k)\).

Lemma (normalized rank monotone). Let \(a+K+d\le D\) and \(1\le K\le n\). Then \(c_P(k)/N_n(k)\) is nonincreasing for \(0\le k\le K\); in particular \(c_P(K-d)\ge\frac{N_n(K-d)}{N_n(K)}c_P(K)\) when \(K\ge d\).

Proof. For \(k\le K\): \(Z_P(k)=Z_P(K)\cap V_k\); \(C_D\cap V_k\subseteq Z_P(k)\) by (M); and \(x\,Z_P(k)\subseteq Z_P(k+1)\) for \(k<K\), since \(Pg_if\in C_D\) has degree at most \(a+d+k\le D-1\). Take a degree-respecting monomial order in which the pivot variables of the reduced affine equations of \(\mathcal Q\), if any, are the largest variables. Let \(\mathcal L\) be the set of leading monomials of nonzero elements of \(Z_P(K)\) and \(\mathcal B\) the monomials of degree at most \(K\) outside \(\mathcal L\); \(\mathcal B\) is a basis of \(V_K/Z_P(K)\), and its elements of degree at most \(k\) are a basis of \(V_k/Z_P(k)\), because an element of \(Z_P(K)\) with leading monomial of degree at most \(k\) lies in \(V_k\). \(\mathcal L\) is closed under multiplication by variables within degree \(K\): if \(f\in Z_P(K)\) has leading monomial of degree at most \(K-1\), then \(\deg f\le K-1\), so \(f\in Z_P(K-1)\), \(xf\in Z_P(K)\), and the leading monomial of \(xf\) is \(x\) times that of \(f\). So \(\mathcal B\) is closed under taking divisors. \(\mathcal L\) contains every \(x_i^2\) when \(K\ge2\), and every pivot variable: sums of the affine axioms lie in \(C_D\) for \(D\ge1\), each row of the reduced system has one pivot variable as its leading monomial, consistency excluding the row \(1\), and \(C_D\cap V_1\subseteq Z_P(K)\) as \(K\ge1\). So \(\mathcal B\) consists of squarefree monomials in the \(n\) non-pivot variables: a family of subsets of an \(n\)-set closed under taking subsets. With \(b_j\) its number of \(j\)-sets, counting pairs of a \((j+1)\)-set of the family and a \(j\)-subset gives \((j+1)b_{j+1}\le(n-j)b_j\), so \(b_j/\binom nj\) is nonincreasing. \(c_P(k)/N_n(k)\) is the average of these ratios for \(j\le k\) with weights \(\binom nj\), and adding a term not above the earlier ones does not raise an average. \(\square\)

Gain. Let \(K\ge d\) and \(a+K+2d\le D\). Then some \(q\in\operatorname{span}\{g_i\}\) has \(c_{P(1+q)}(K)\le c_P(K)-\tfrac12c_P(K-d)\).

Proof. On \(V_{K-d}\) let \(M_if=([Pg_\alpha g_if])_\alpha\). The stacked kernel is \(Z_P(K-d)\): if \(f\in Z_P(K-d)\), \(Pg_\alpha f\in C_D\) has degree at most \(a+K\) and (M) applies with \(g_i\); conversely \(Pg_i^2f\in C_D\) and \(P(g_i^2+g_i)f\in C_D\) by (B) and (M), degree \(a+K+d\), give \(Pg_if\in C_D\). So \(\operatorname{rank}\overline M=c_P(K-d)\). Apply rank retention with \(h_\alpha=Pg_\alpha\), \(b=a+d\), the \(g_i\) of degree at most \(d\), \(k=K-d\): \(b+k+2d=a+K+2d\le D\). It gives \(q=\sum c_ig_i\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(f\mapsto([Pg_\alpha qf])_\alpha)\ge\tfrac12c_P(K-d)\) on \(V_{K-d}\), that is \(\dim(qV_{K-d}+Z_P(K))/Z_P(K)\ge\tfrac12c_P(K-d)\). With \(P'=P(1+q)\): \(Z_P(K)\subseteq Z_{P'}(K)\) by (M), degree \(a+d+K+d\); and for \(f\in V_{K-d}\), \(P'g_iqf=Pg_if(q+q^2)\in C_D\) by (B) and (M), degree \(a+d+K-d+2d\). So \(\dim Z_{P'}(K)\ge\dim Z_P(K)+\tfrac12c_P(K-d)\). \(\square\)

Theorem (binary approximator rank). Let \(1\le d\le K\le n\), \(t\ge1\) and \(dt+K+d\le D\). For every family \(g_1,\ldots,g_s\) of degree at most \(d\) there are \(q_1,\ldots,q_t\in\operatorname{span}\{g_i\}\) such that \(P=\prod_{j\le t}(1+q_j)\) satisfies

\[c_P(K)\ \le\ h_K\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\frac{N_n(K-d)}{N_n(K)}\Bigr)^{t},\qquad h_K=\dim V_K/(C_D\cap V_K).\]

Proof. For \(P=1\), \(C_D\cap V_K\subseteq Z_1(K)\) by (M), so \(c_1(K)\le h_K\). In round \(j\le t\) the current product has degree \(a\le(j-1)d\); the lemma applies, as \(a+K+d\le D\), and the gain, as \(a+K+2d\le(j+1)d+K\le dt+K+d\). Together \(c_{P(1+q)}(K)\le c_P(K)\bigl(1-\tfrac12N_n(K-d)/N_n(K)\bigr)\). \(\square\)

This is the statement imported in the bounded-depth transfer entry, with the free dimension included. The hypothesis \(1\notin C_D\) is not needed for it; it is used in the leveled lemma, where \(h_K>0\) is needed.

The transfer as one statement

Theorem (near-half Frege transfer). Fix a Frege system \(F\) in the DeMorgan language, a depth \(d\ge1\) and \(A>0\), and let \(c_F\) be the constant of the simulation, \(\ell=d+c_F\). For each \(n\) in an infinite set let \(F_n\) be a CNF of width \(w_n\) and \(\Lambda_n\) a set of affine equations over \(\mathbb F_2\) with \(n=v_n-\operatorname{rank}\Lambda_n\), \(v_n\) the number of variables of \(F_n\) and \(\Lambda_n\) together, such that the polynomial system of the clause polynomials of \(F_n\), the Boolean axioms and \(\Lambda_n\) has no polynomial calculus refutation of degree \(\lfloor n/2-s_n\rfloor\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), where \(s_n\ge0\) and \((s_n+w_n)(\log n)^{\ell-2}=o(n)\); here \(\ell\ge2\), and \(\Lambda_n\) is consistent because the system has no refutation. Then for all large \(n\), \(F_n\) has no \(F_d(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\)-refutation with at most \(n^A\) symbols.

Proof. The Frege parity size bound, whose only condition was the theorem just proved. \(\square\)

Scope. As in the simulation entry: \(p=2\); Frege formulations; refutations as sequences of formulas from the clauses ending in \(0\); size in symbols; \(c_F\) not computed. The proofs of this chain are working proofs and none is formalized; their reviews are recorded in each entry's verification gate.

Specification decision. No change. The transfer's requirements were recorded in the two preceding entries; proving the imported theorem adds none and removes none.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer checked every step by hand as a proof, with the paper used only for comparison, and found no mathematical error: the two standard facts and extension of scalars; the multiplicity sum and its induction; the determinant argument; descent and the kernel step; all degrees in the multiplication-map step and the assembly of the specialization; both kernel inclusions and the factorization in the gain; the rounds of the theorem and that \(c_P(K)\) does not depend on the degree bound used; and that the theorem matches the statement imported earlier. Its corrections were of precision and are applied: which affine set defines the free dimension; the transfer theorem's \(n\), exponent and consistency; one sentence each in the descent step, the closure of leading monomials and the pivots; the limits attached to "discharged". Unused: \(K\le n\) beyond positivity of weights, and \(1\notin C_D\). The reviewer did not re-verify the three earlier entries of the chain, each of which had its own review. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing. The independent check queued by the simulation entry is carried out here as a full proof. The item's other queued checks, a quantitative size bound and the composition of the older block route, are optional for the goal; the next entry returns to the family.

What the family must now satisfy

Read off thm:near-half-frege-transfer. For depth \(d\), with \(\ell=d+c_F\): a literal CNF \(F_n\) of width \(w_n\), with auxiliary affine equations \(\Lambda_n\) that are not part of the formula, free dimension \(n\), no polynomial calculus refutation over \(\mathbb F_2\) of degree \(\lfloor n/2-s_n\rfloor\), and \((s_n+w_n)(\log n)^{\ell-2}=o(n)\); for all depths at once, \(s_n+w_n\le n^{1-\epsilon}\); formula length polynomial in \(n\).

Specification revision, under the notebook's rule that a weakened requirement is matched by a weakened specification. Dropped, as no longer asked by any step: the product-only grammar, coherent profiles and block ledgers of the older route; the preference for constant width, and the condition \(2w\le D_v\) as a transfer condition. Changed: the width is paid in the deficit budget. Tightened: the deficit exponent is \(\ell-2\) with \(\ell=d+c_F\ge d+1\), so a deficit of order \(n/\log n\) serves no depth \(d\ge1\). Kept: the necessary conditions for the degree hypothesis recorded in the accepted specification, which the transfer does not touch. The balanced paired modular source has the actual ceiling \(v/2-(8/9-o(1))v/k\) on its original instances, which have no affine rows, so \(v\) is their free dimension, with \(k=O(\log v)\): a deficit at least of order \(v/\log v\), excluded by the tightened exponent for every depth. Its selected cores are not bounded by that ceiling and are not excluded by this argument. Obstacle

One thing: no lower-bound method for polynomial calculus over \(\mathbb F_2\) reaches \(n/2-n^{1-\epsilon}\) of any dimension for a polynomial-size CNF, and no such formula is known. Since the transfer is ours, the place where the dimension enters is known exactly: one counting inequality on the family of standard monomials of the kernels, \((j+1)b_{j+1}\le(n-j)b_j\). Whether some formula has a proper closure at half of a smaller effective dimension, defined by the actual sizes of those levels, is the recorded thin-kernel alternative; nothing new is known about its attainability.

Architecture review

Necessary target. As stated above: a polynomial-length literal CNF with a degree barrier at \(\lfloor n/2-s\rfloor\) of the free dimension, \(s+w\le n^{1-\epsilon}\) for all depths, or \((s+w)(\log n)^{d+c_F-2}=o(n)\) for depth \(d\).

Extra requirements. The search has asked for \(n\) to be the free dimension. The proof needs less: its rate holds whenever the levels of the standard monomials in the window below the cutoff are at most \(\binom Xj\), by the Kruskal–Katona argument already recorded, with \(X\) in place of \(n\). This weaker endpoint is not adopted as the target, because no formula is known to have thin levels with a proper closure at \(X/2\) and a recorded necessary condition, no shattered set larger than about \(2K\), has no known mechanism; it is kept as an alternative whose statement now follows from proofs in this notebook.

Independent alternative. Given only the goal, the transfer and the recorded facts about the family, the reviewer proposed three options (record): a generic count by the series \((1+z)^n/\prod(1+z^{k_i})\), with the heuristic that barely covering mixed-width systems on dense forms sit near half; an extension-count version of the transfer tested on the pigeonhole principle; and nonlinear auxiliary definitions with thin levels. It advised against settling the half term as a separate project. Compared with the route held before, developing the queue's head toward a family: all three are different, and the first two had tests cheap enough to run in this cycle.

  • Series count. Computed exactly (uniform widths, mixed widths): at covering density \(m=\lceil\ln2\cdot2^kn\rceil\) with \(k=2,3,4,6\) the index over \(n\) is \(0.05\) to \(0.17\) at \(n=1024\), rising with \(k\) and falling with \(n\); for uniform widths \(\log_2n\) and \(\log_2n+2\) with \(\sum_i2^{-k_i}=1\) it is \(0.35\) at \(n=256,512,1024\), and for four mixed pairs of widths with the same sum, computed at \(n=256\) and \(1024\), between \(0.345\) and \(0.363\); with sum \(4\) it is \(0.32\). For widths of at least \(\log_2n-3\) the index in these data depends on the covering sum and not on the widths; at small fixed width it is much lower at the same or larger sum. The reviewer's estimate of a third for uniform width is not supported for \(k\le6\), and its estimate near half for barely covering profiles is falsified. Test. Falsified for the profiles sampled, which do not exhaust polynomial-size profiles: the index is a constant fraction below half. This concerns the series. That generic systems follow it is the untested semi-regularity hypothesis; the index is no ceiling for structured systems; and the proposed bound "degree at most index plus \(O(k)\)" was not tested.
  • Pigeonhole with extension counts. Standard monomials of the matching ideal are partial matchings, \(b_j=\binom mj\binom njj!\), so \(b_{j-1}/b_j=j/((m-j+1)(n-j+1))\), about \(2/n\) at \(j=n/2\), \(m=n+1\); the top level dominates the cumulative sums, so the rate per factor at input degree one is of order \(1/n\), and of order \(n\) factors are needed at the first level, above the cutoff \(n/2\). Test. Falsified for the matching-ideal levels: the engine needs a rate that is not polynomially small. The kernels of the proof contain the closure and may have thinner levels, which this estimate does not examine.
  • Nonlinear definitions with thin levels. On inspection the proof of the rank theorem uses the affine equations only in the one count, so the transfer should hold with \(X\) in place of \(n\) when the window levels are at most \(\binom Xj\); this is not yet written as a proof and is the sub-idea below. Test. Passed on inspection, unproved; it is the thin-kernel alternative above and supplies no formula. The reviewer's control, for the proved theorem: Tseitin modulo two and counting modulo two have refutations of constant degree over \(\mathbb F_2\), hence no barrier, and the theorem says nothing about them.

Rank normalization. This is the block's one structural finding on that question: the loss per factor is measured relative to the level sizes of the standard monomials, not to the ambient cube, and relative contraction by the actual levels can replace the binomial ratio. It is the content of the weaker endpoint above.

Decision. Keep the target and the engine. Generic covering systems stay set aside, now with the series computation as a reason within its hypothesis. Do not open the half-term question as a project. The line has no candidate; the next cycles develop queued leads against the revised requirement, and a request is filed in user_requests on whether the draining order should yield to work chosen for the family.

The system to try it on is the guarded width-five witness, whose closure is known to be proper at a positive linear degree. 9 October 2026 — Compatible combinations of local sections are the Nullstellensatz dual; no test of properness found in that form

No new result: the lead's criterion is identified with a known duality, and a single functional is shown unable to certify properness. Queue development of the local sections lead while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement, the queue's head is the local sections and cohomology lead of the first architecture review: a criterion of Abramsky–Mansfield–Barbosa, as that review read it, says an obstruction vanishes exactly when there is a compatible family of linear combinations of local sections. Does this give a condition for a proper closure at degree \(D\) that is not properness restated?

Architecture test. Outcome of the decisive test named in the transfer-done review: no criterion beyond the static one was found in the form tried, and the lead is not closed. Over \(\mathbb F_2\) at level \(D\), a compatible family of odd-mass combinations of local sections on all sets of at most \(D\) variables is the same thing as a linear functional that is one at \(1\) and vanishes on all multiples of the axioms within degree \(D\): the dual of a Nullstellensatz refutation, by the same linear duality as the recorded local design criterion. It is implied by properness of the polynomial calculus closure and I do not have the converse. A single functional cannot do more: if its kernel is closed under multiplication by variables below degree \(D\), it is evaluation at a satisfying assignment. A certificate of properness in this language must therefore be a family of maps, not one family of weights; that form, the pseudo-reduction operator, was not tried here. The guarded witness was not examined.

New mathematics. None registered: the identification, written out so that the lead's language and the record's are matched, and the elementary remark that a functional with closed kernel is a point evaluation.

Goal progress. Unchanged. A necessary condition in other words, and no method.

General statement. The identification is the duality of prop:local-design-criterion with the static span in place of its truncated ideals, the two agreeing when each constraint forbids one assignment; the open implication is unchanged and is the family statement itself.

The identification

Let the system consist of constraints in canonical encoding, constraint \(a\) on the variable set \(U_a\) with axioms the indicators \(\chi\) of its forbidden assignments, of degree \(|U_a|\), together with the Boolean axioms; work with multilinear polynomials. For a set \(U\) of at most \(D\) variables, a local section on \(U\) is an assignment to \(U\) violating no constraint with \(U_a\subseteq U\).

A linear functional \(\varphi\) on multilinear polynomials of degree at most \(D\) is the same as a family \((\mu_U)_{|U|\le D}\), \(\mu_U:\{0,1\}^U\to\mathbb F_2\), compatible under restriction: put \(\mu_U(\alpha)=\varphi(\chi^U_\alpha)\), the value on the indicator of \(\alpha\), a polynomial of degree \(|U|\); conversely \(\varphi(g)=\sum_\alpha\mu_U(\alpha)g(\alpha)\) for \(g\) on \(U\), extended linearly over monomials, and compatibility, \(\mu_W(\beta)=\sum_{\alpha|_W=\beta}\mu_U(\alpha)\) for \(W\subseteq U\), is what makes this independent of \(U\), by \(\chi^W_\beta=\sum_{\alpha|_W=\beta}\chi^U_\alpha\). Then \(\varphi(1)=1\) says that each \(\mu_U\) has odd mass, and \(\varphi(m\chi)=0\) for every axiom \(\chi\) of a constraint \(a\) and every monomial \(m\) with \(|U_a\cup\operatorname{supp}m|\le D\) says that \(\mu_U\) vanishes on assignments violating \(a\), for every \(U\supseteq U_a\) with \(|U|\le D\): indeed \(m\chi\) is zero or has multilinear degree exactly \(|U_a\cup\operatorname{supp}m|\), its multilinear form is a sum of indicators on \(U=U_a\cup\operatorname{supp}m\) of assignments violating \(a\), and every such indicator lies in the span of these products; products that are not multilinear reduce to these within the same degree. So the functionals that are one at \(1\) and vanish on the multiples of the axioms within degree \(D\) are exactly the compatible families of odd-mass \(\mathbb F_2\)-combinations of local sections. Such a functional exists exactly when \(1\) is not a combination of those multiples, which is the absence of a Nullstellensatz refutation of degree \(D\) in this encoding.

The closure \(C_D\) contains those multiples, so \(1\notin C_D\) implies that such a family exists. The closure also contains, for every element \(p\) of degree below \(D\) obtained with cancellation of leading terms, the products \(x_ip\). Could one functional account for that through its kernel? No. Suppose \(\varphi(1)=1\) and \(\varphi(p)=0\), \(\deg p\le D-1\), implies \(\varphi(x_ip)=0\) for all \(i\). For a monomial \(m\) of degree at most \(D-1\), \(m+\varphi(m)\) lies in the kernel, so \(\varphi(x_im)=\varphi(x_i)\varphi(m)\); hence \(\varphi(x_S)=\prod_{i\in S}\varphi(x_i)\) for \(|S|\le D\), and \(\varphi\) is evaluation at the point \((\varphi(x_i))_i\), which satisfies every axiom of degree at most \(D\) that \(\varphi\) kills. So for an unsatisfiable system the proper closed subspace \(C_D\) is never the kernel of a functional closed in this sense: a witness of properness has corank larger than one, and in the language of sections it is a compatible family of linear maps between spaces of combinations of local sections, a pseudo-reduction \(R\) with \(R(1)=1\), \(R\) zero on axioms and \(R(x_it)=R(x_iR(t))\), and not a single compatible family of weights. That formulation is the next attempt on this lead.

The source's statement is as read in the first architecture review, anchored at one section and for abelian groups; I did not reread it in this cycle. The unanchored mass-one form above is what applies to refutations, and it holds over any field.

9 October 2026 — The transfer with the level-size dimension: thin top levels can replace the free dimension, with explicit parameters

Working proof assembling recorded results; the thin-kernel alternative now has a proved transfer, and its attainability is as open as before. Queue development of a chosen check while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Chosen. This check bears on the family statement, the one open statement: it turns the only recorded alternative to "half the free dimension" into a proved requirement, so that a candidate with thin standard-monomial levels can be judged against an exact condition; the head, the local sections lead, has no such direct bearing until its operator form is written.

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: the review noted, on inspection only, that the transfer should hold with the level sizes of the closure's standard monomials in place of the free dimension. State it and prove it.

New mathematics. An assembly, with no new idea: in the rank theorem the count on standard monomials is replaced by the recorded Kruskal–Katona growth lemma, and the bounded-depth transfer and its simulation go through unchanged. The result is non-asymptotic: for a refutation with at most \(S\) gates, a cutoff \(K\) and a real \(X\) bounding the levels in a window of polylogarithmic width below \(K\), with \(X\) at most about \((2+1/\delta)(K-\delta)\).

Goal progress. Unchanged. The family statement is as open as before; its alternative endpoint now has a proved transfer in the same proof systems as the main one, and nothing is known about whether any formula meets it.

General statement. thm:level-size-degree-transfer and cor:level-size-size-bound hold for every CNF, every set of affine equations, every number of levels and all parameters satisfying the displayed conditions.

Setting and the rate

As in the rank theorem entry: \(C_D\) is the degree-\(D\) closure over \(\mathbb F_2\) of a set containing the Boolean axioms, and \(\mathfrak M_0\) the set of standard monomials of \(C_D\) of degree at most \(K\) for a degree-respecting order, with \(m_j(\mathfrak M_0)=\dim V_j/(C_D\cap V_j)-\dim V_{j-1}/(C_D\cap V_{j-1})\) its number in degree \(j\), independent of the order. For a real \(X\) and integers \(1\le\delta\le K\) put \(\rho_\delta=(X-K+\delta)/(K-\delta+1)\) and \(\theta_\delta=(1+\sum_{i=1}^\delta\rho_\delta^i)^{-1}\).

Rank with level sizes. Let \(1\le d\le K\), \(t\ge1\), \(dt+K+d\le D\), and \(X\ge K\) real with \(m_j(\mathfrak M_0)\le\binom Xj\) for \(K-d<j\le K\). Then for every family \(g_1,\ldots,g_s\) of degree at most \(d\) there is \(P=\prod_{j\le t}(1+q_j)\), \(q_j\in\operatorname{span}\{g_i\}\), with \(c_P(K)\le h_K(1-\tfrac12\theta_d)^t\).

Proof. As for the rank theorem, with one change. In round \(j\) the product has degree \(a\le(j-1)d\), and the gain step gives \(c_{P(1+q)}(K)\le c_P(K)-\tfrac12c_P(K-d)\), its condition \(a+K+2d\le D\) holding as before. The Kruskal–Katona growth lemma, whose hypotheses are \(a+d+K\le D\), \(1\le\delta\le K\), \(X\ge K\) and the level bound on \(K-\delta<j\le K\), applied with \(\delta=d\), gives \(c_P(K-d)\ge\theta_dc_P(K)\); the kernels and the down-closed family of that lemma are those of the rank theorem's proof. \(\square\)

The transfer

Theorem (level-size degree transfer). Let \(F\) be a CNF of width \(w\), \(\Lambda\) a set of affine equations over \(\mathbb F_2\), and \(C_D\) the closure of the clause polynomials, Boolean axioms and \(\Lambda\), with \(1\notin C_D\). Let \(t_1,\ldots,t_\ell\ge1\), \(\Delta_0=1\), \(\Delta_i=\Delta_{i-1}t_i\), \(\Delta=\Delta_\ell\), and \(K\) with \(\Delta_{\ell-1}\le K\) and \(K+\max\{4\Delta,\Delta+w\}\le D\). Let \(X\ge K\) be real with \(m_j(\mathfrak M_0)\le\binom Xj\) for \(K-\Delta_{\ell-1}<j\le K\). Then every refutation of \(F\) with at most \(\ell\) levels in the sequent system of the bounded-depth transfer theorem, with multiset parity, satisfies \(\sum_{i=1}^\ell S_i\bigl(1-\tfrac12\theta_{\Delta_{i-1}}\bigr)^{t_i}\ge1\).

Proof. The proof of the bounded-depth transfer theorem uses the rank theorem only through the leveled lemma, and that lemma uses it only as a bound \(c_P(K)\le h_K(1-\eta)^{t_i}\) for each family of level \(i\), with members of degree at most \(\Delta_{i-1}\). Replace that bound by the one above with \(d=\Delta_{i-1}\), \(t=t_i\): its conditions hold, \(\Delta_{i-1}\le\Delta_{\ell-1}\le K\), \(\Delta_i+K+\Delta_{i-1}\le D\), and the window \(K-\Delta_{i-1}<j\le K\) lies in the window of the hypothesis. The rest of both proofs is unchanged. \(\square\)

Corollary (level-size size bound). Let \(\ell\ge1\), \(S\ge2\), \(\Theta=\ln(\ell S)\), and define \(\Delta_0=1\), \(t_i=\lceil2(1+e\Delta_{i-1})\Theta\rceil+1\), \(\Delta_i=\Delta_{i-1}t_i\), \(\delta^*=\Delta_{\ell-1}\), \(\Delta=\Delta_\ell\). In the setting of the theorem, with \(1\notin C_D\), suppose \(\delta^*\le K\), \(K+\max\{4\Delta,\Delta+w\}\le D\), and a real \(X\ge K\) has

\[m_j(\mathfrak M_0)\le\binom Xj\ \ (K-\delta^*<j\le K),\qquad X\le2(K-\delta^*)+1+\frac{K-\delta^*+1}{\delta^*}.\]

Then \(F\) has no refutation with at most \(\ell\) levels and at most \(S\) disjunctions and lines in that system; and for a Frege system \(F'\) and depth \(r\) with \(\ell=r+c_{F'}\), no \(F'_r(\mathrm{MOD}_2)\)-refutation with at most \((S/c_{F'})^{1/3}\) symbols.

Proof. For \(\delta\le\delta^*\), \(\rho_\delta\le\rho_{\delta^*}\le1+1/\delta^*\), the first because the numerator of \(\rho_\delta\) increases and its denominator decreases with \(\delta\), the second being the displayed bound on \(X\). So \(\sum_{i\le\delta}\rho_\delta^i\le\delta(1+1/\delta^*)^{\delta^*}\le e\delta\) and \(\theta_\delta\ge1/(1+e\delta)\). With \(\delta=\Delta_{i-1}\): \((1-\tfrac12\theta)^{t_i}\le\exp(-t_i/(2(1+e\Delta_{i-1})))<e^{-\Theta}=1/(\ell S)\). So \(\sum_iS_i(1-\tfrac12\theta_{\Delta_{i-1}})^{t_i}<1/\ell\le1\) when \(\sum_iS_i\le S\), against the theorem. The last statement is the simulation, which turns \(s\) symbols into at most \(c_{F'}s^3\) disjunctions and lines. \(\square\)

What it asks of a formula

The degrees are \(\Delta_1\approx2(1+e)\Theta\) and \(\Delta_i\approx2e\Theta\Delta_{i-1}^2\), polylogarithmic in \(S\) for fixed \(\ell\), growing doubly exponentially in \(\ell\). The condition on \(X\) says that the cutoff \(K\) is at least about \(X/2-X/(4\delta^*)+\delta^*\): a barrier within \(X/\operatorname{polylog}(S)\) of half the level-size dimension \(X\), at \(D=K+O(\Delta)+w\). With \(X=n\), the free dimension, and \(n\ge K\), the level bound always holds: \(\Lambda\) is consistent because \(1\notin C_D\); for \(P=1\) and the order with pivots largest, the rank theorem's proof shows the standard monomials of the kernel, which lies between \(C_D\cap V_K\) and \(V_K\), to be squarefree in the non-pivot variables, the same argument applies to \(C_D\cap V_K\) itself, and \(m_j\) does not depend on the order. This gives a version of the main transfer with explicit parameters and a deficit of order \(n/\delta^*\); since \(\delta^*\) is about \(\Theta^{2^{\ell-1}-1}\), it admits a smaller deficit than the binomial version at every \(\ell\ge2\), and it is not asymptotic.

For \(X<n\) the hypothesis is the thin-kernel endpoint: the closure must be proper at about \(X/2\) while its standard monomials in the window number at most \(\binom Xj\). The recorded necessary condition stands, every set of variables shattered by the closure through degree \(K\) has size at most about \(2K\), and no formula is known to meet the endpoint with \(X\) below its free dimension. The level sizes are those of the closure with \(\Lambda\) included.

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement, the preceding entry on this lead showed that one compatible family of weights on local sections cannot certify a proper closure and named the operator form as the next attempt: a linear map \(R\) with \(R(1)=1\), \(R\) zero on axioms and \(R(x_it)=R(x_iR(t))\). Does that form, read as compatible linear maps of local sections, give a condition that is neither properness restated nor a method already in the record?

New mathematics. None. The equivalence of the operator with a proper closure is written out with both directions; the local version is identified with the expansion method read earlier in this notebook.

Goal progress. Unchanged. With no locality the lead's operator is properness restated, and with boundary-closure neighbourhoods it is a construction already read; other neighbourhoods are not examined.

General statement. No new all-parameter claim; the statements used are the standard operator criterion, proved below for completeness, and prop:two-occurrence-expansion-ceiling, which caps the stated bounds of the two expansion theorems and not every local construction.

The operator criterion

Work with multilinear polynomials over a field, \(V_D\) those of degree at most \(D\), a system containing the Boolean axioms, and \(C_D\) its closure. Call \(R:V_D\to V_D\) a reduction if it is linear, \(R(1)=1\), \(R(a)=0\) for every axiom \(a\) of degree at most \(D\), \(R(V_{D-1})\subseteq V_{D-1}\), and \(R(x_it)=R(x_iR(t))\) for every variable \(x_i\) and every term \(t\) of degree at most \(D-1\), products being reduced to multilinear form, which keeps them within degree \(D\).

If \(1\notin C_D\), a reduction exists: fix a degree-respecting order and let \(R(p)\) be the remainder of \(p\) modulo \(C_D\cap V_D\), the unique polynomial in the span of the standard monomials congruent to \(p\). It is linear, kills \(C_D\), does not raise degree, and fixes \(1\), which is a standard monomial because \(1\notin C_D\); for a term \(t\) of degree at most \(D-1\), \(t-R(t)\in C_D\) has degree at most \(D-1\), so \(x_i(t-R(t))\in C_D\) and \(R(x_it)=R(x_iR(t))\). Conversely, if a reduction exists, then \(C_D\subseteq\ker R\): the axioms are in the kernel, the kernel is a subspace, and for \(p\in\ker R\cap V_{D-1}\), by linearity over the terms of \(p\), \(R(x_ip)=R(x_iR(p))=0\); so \(1\notin C_D\). Thus the operator form, when \(R\) is not required to be local, is properness of the closure restated. The sufficiency is the criterion used in the degree lower-bound literature; the converse is elementary and I have not looked for a source.

The local form

In the language of sections, \(R\) is local if \(R(t)\), for a term \(t\) on a set \(U\) of variables, is determined by the local sections of a neighbourhood \(\operatorname{Cl}(U)\): \(R(t)\) is the remainder of \(t\) modulo the ideal of the constraints inside \(\operatorname{Cl}(U)\), an ideal of functions vanishing on those local sections. The identity \(R(x_it)=R(x_iR(t))\) then follows from a statement that the remainder does not change when the neighbourhood is enlarged. This is the operator of Alekhnovich and Razborov's Theorem 3.13 as read in the private-direction entry: there the neighbourhood is a closure under small boundary, and independence of the neighbourhood is proved by eliminating a row through a variable private to it. The expansion ceiling caps the bound stated in that theorem at \(v/4+s/2\) for rows on variables with every variable in at least two rows; it does not cap every local construction, and that entry notes that a theorem without the factor one half is not excluded. For rows on linear forms the recorded scope is that the stated leading-term analogue and operators on the monomial basis fail; other bases are not excluded.

So the lead, in operator form, is that construction when the neighbourhoods are boundary closures, and properness itself when \(R\) is not local. A different notion of neighbourhood with a proof of independence would be a new lower-bound method. Whether the record already contains one is what the test on the guarded witness would decide: its degree bound is inherited from an earlier linear-degree witness, whose proof I did not reread in this cycle. That test is still owed.

In the local form: the ceiling caps the stated bound of Theorem 3.13 and not every local construction; the cap for the immunity theorem is not attributed to this operator; independence of the neighbourhood implies the identity and is not the identity; the scope for linear forms is the recorded one. With the transfer proved for literal CNFs, the question is which polynomial systems can be presented as such a CNF with auxiliary affine equations, without changing the free dimension.

New mathematics. A system of clauses on affine forms over \(\mathbb F_2^n\), each clause forbidding one tuple of values of at most \(w\) forms, is presented by a literal CNF of width \(\max\{w,3\}\) and polynomial length, with affine equations defining the forms, of free dimension \(n\), such that a degree barrier for the original system gives the hypothesis of the transfer. So the cost of such axioms is their width, paid in the deficit budget. Axioms that are not single clauses on forms are not covered.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The family statement is restated in a form free of encodings: a polynomial number of clauses on affine forms over \(\mathbb F_2^n\), of width at most \(n^{1-\epsilon}\), with no polynomial calculus refutation within \(n^{1-\epsilon}\) of degree \(n/2\). No such system is known.

General statement. prop:form-clause-encoding holds for every finite system of clauses on affine forms over \(\mathbb F_2\) and every degree \(D\ge\max\{w,3\}\).

Statement and proof

A clause on forms is a pair \((\ell,b)\) of affine forms \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\) on \(\mathbb F_2^n\), \(k\le w\), and \(b\in\mathbb F_2^k\); it forbids the points with \(\ell(x)=b\), and its polynomial is \(\prod_j(\ell_j+b_j+1)\), of degree at most \(k\). Let \(G\) be a system of \(m\) such clauses, with the Boolean axioms of \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\).

Proposition (form clause encoding). There are a literal CNF \(F\) and a set \(\Lambda\) of affine equations over \(\mathbb F_2\), on \(v\le n+mwn\) variables, with at most \(m+4mwn\) clauses of width at most \(\max\{w,3\}\), such that: \(\Lambda\) is consistent of rank \(v-n\); \(F\) is unsatisfiable if and only if \(G\) is; and for every \(D\ge\max\{w,3\}\), the clause polynomials of \(F\), the Boolean axioms and \(\Lambda\) have a polynomial calculus refutation of degree \(D\) if and only if \(G\) has one.

Proof. First remove constant forms: a factor with \(\ell_j\) constant is dropped from its clause when \(\ell_j=b_j\), the clause is dropped when \(\ell_j\ne b_j\), and if a clause loses all its factors \(G\) contains \(1\) and \(F\) is the empty clause; none of this changes the clause polynomials. For each remaining form \(\ell=c+\sum_{i\in T}x_i\) occurring in \(G\), with \(T=\{i_1<\cdots<i_t\}\), introduce variables \(z_1,\ldots,z_t\) and the equations \(z_1=x_{i_1}+c\), \(z_r=z_{r-1}+x_{i_r}\); the last variable \(y=z_t\) equals \(\ell\) on their solutions. \(\Lambda\) is the set of these equations; each has its own new variable as pivot, so \(\Lambda\) is consistent of rank the number of new variables, at most \(mwn\). \(F\) consists of, for each equation on at most three variables, its at most four clauses of width at most three, and for each clause \((\ell,b)\) of \(G\) the literal clause forbidding \(y=b\) on the corresponding variables, of width \(k\).

The assignments satisfying the definitional clauses are those satisfying \(\Lambda\), and on them the clause on \(y\) is violated exactly when \(\ell(x)=b\); so \(F\) and \(G\) are equisatisfiable. For the degrees: each definitional clause polynomial is the indicator \(Q\) of one assignment to three variables \(z,a,b'\) violating \(e=z+a+b'+c'\), and for the violating point \(p=(p_1,p_2,p_3)\) it is the multilinear form of \((a+p_2+1)(b'+p_3+1)\,e\): both are functions of three Boolean variables equal to one exactly at \(p\), since \(e=1\) fixes \(z\) once \(a,b'\) are given. For the equation on two variables, \(Q\) is the multilinear form of \((x+p_2+1)e\). So with \(\Lambda\) present the definitional clauses are derived within degree three and can be dropped for \(D\ge3\). By the free-dimension lemma, lem:affine-free-dimension, for \(D\ge2\) and at least the axiom degrees, the system of the remaining clause polynomials, Boolean axioms and \(\Lambda\) has a refutation of degree \(D\) if and only if the system obtained by substituting \(\Lambda\) away has one; that substitution replaces each \(y\) by its form \(\ell\), turns the literal clause polynomial into \(\prod_j(\ell_j+b_j+1)\), and turns the Boolean axioms of the new variables into \(\ell^2+\ell\), which the Boolean axioms of \(x\) derive in degree two. The substituted system is \(G\). \(\square\)

Consequence. If \(G_n\) on \(\mathbb F_2^n\) has polynomially many clauses on at most \(w_n\) forms each and no refutation of degree \(\lfloor n/2-s_n\rfloor\), then for large \(n\), when that degree is at least three, \(F_n\), \(\Lambda_n\) satisfy the hypotheses of thm:near-half-frege-transfer with free dimension \(n\), width \(\max\{w_n,3\}\) and the same \(s_n\); the formula length is polynomial in \(n\), so the conclusion is a superpolynomial bound in the length. The answer to the check: a clause on \(w\) affine forms, of polynomial degree \(w\), is admitted at the cost \(w\) in the budget \(s+w\). A relation forbidding several tuples of values of one tuple of forms is admitted as that many clauses, but the barrier must then be proved for the system of the separate clauses, which is stronger than the single axiom that is their sum: recovering one clause from the sum costs degree up to \(2w\). Sums of products on different forms, sparse polynomials among them, are not covered here.

The family statement in pure form

Conversely, a literal CNF of width \(w\) with affine equations of free dimension \(n\) becomes, on substituting the equations, a system of clauses on at most \(w\) affine forms of the free variables, with the same refutation degrees from \(\max\{w,2\}\) on by the same lemma. So the first open statement is equivalent to the following, with no encoding in it: for infinitely many \(n\), at most \(n^{O(1)}\) affine subspaces of codimension at most \(n^{1-\epsilon}\) covering \(\mathbb F_2^n\), such that their indicator polynomials, with the Boolean axioms, do not generate \(1\) within degree \(n/2-n^{1-\epsilon}\); for one depth \(d\), deficit and codimension \(o(n/(\log n)^{d+c_F-2})\) suffice. The recorded constraints on such covers stand: a cover by \(m\) subspaces has one of codimension at most \(\log_2m\); full independence of many rows forces many rows and slack; and the series index of generic covers is about \(0.35n\).

Specification decision. The specification's objects are widened to match: rows may be clauses on affine forms of width up to the budget, presented as above; the accepted conditions, stated for relations on variables, apply to the presented CNF and are not re-derived for forms here. No property is dropped beyond those the last review dropped.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer, checking by hand against the free-dimension lemma, found no error in the construction, the counts, the rank, equisatisfiability or the use of the lemma. Corrections applied: constant forms are removed first; the degree step exhibits the product equal to each definitional clause polynomial; the consequence is stated for large \(n\); my sentence that a sum of products is admitted as several clauses was wrong as written, since splitting strengthens the axioms, and the remark about auxiliary variables was unproved and is removed; the pure form names indicator polynomials of subspaces and has its converse. Not verified by the reviewer: the transfer theorem's clause-polynomial convention from its summary, and the second and third recorded constraints. Unused: \(D\ge w\) in the direction from the CNF to \(G\). Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Developed. The check asked whether axioms of degree \(n^\epsilon\) with short descriptions are admitted and at what cost: by prop:form-clause-encoding with thm:near-half-frege-transfer, clauses on affine forms are, at the cost of their width. Sums of products on different forms, sparse polynomials among them, are not answered; no candidate uses such axioms, so nothing is queued for them.

Process assessment. A queued check answered with a short proposition, chosen ahead of the head for its bearing on the family. It queues nothing new.
