9 October 2026 — Review: the family statement as a covering problem, six entries without progress on it, and why symmetric axioms cannot help over the binary field

Route review, ordinary scope: one open statement. One lemma from the review itself, on systems of individually symmetric axioms over the binary field; the next test is fixed. No outside leads or bridges while the queue drains. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: what did the six entries since the fifth review obtain, what does the goal still need, and which test comes next?

Architecture test. The test named by the fifth review, the operator form of the local sections lead on the witness, was carried out in the block: the operator is properness when not local, and the witness's proof uses a boundary neighbourhood. It changed no required implication.

New mathematics. One lemma, found when the reviewer broke the test I had drafted: an unsatisfiable system of symmetric polynomials over \(\mathbb F_2\) with axioms of degree at most \(d\le(n+1)/2\) is refuted in degree at most \(3d-1\). So a system of individually symmetric axioms, the shape of the subset-sum system, cannot give a barrier near half with low-degree axioms in characteristic two. Systems symmetric only as a set, such as an orbit of non-symmetric axioms, are not covered.

Goal progress. Unchanged, for the sixth entry in a row. The family statement is open and no method reaching half is known. What changed is its form and the bookkeeping around it, not the implication.

General statement. The line's general claim is the conjunction of thm:near-half-frege-transfer, proved, with the open family statement, which by prop:form-clause-encoding reads: for infinitely many \(n\), polynomially many affine subspaces of \(\mathbb F_2^n\) of codimension at most \(n^{1-\epsilon}\) cover \(\mathbb F_2^n\), and their indicator polynomials with the Boolean axioms do not generate \(1\) within degree \(n/2-n^{1-\epsilon}\).

What the block did

Three entries developed the local sections lead: its criterion is the static dual, its operator form is properness itself when not local and the expansion construction for boundary neighbourhoods, and the witness's degree proof is of that boundary kind. No new mathematics came of it. Two entries developed chosen checks: the transfer with the level-size dimension, thm:level-size-degree-transfer, and the encoding of clauses on affine forms, prop:form-clause-encoding. The audit closed nineteen queued items and corrected the fifth review: a deficit of order \(n/\log n\) is excluded only for \(d+c_F\ge3\).

That correction matters little for the goal, which asks for every fixed depth: a family with such a deficit serves at most the depths with \(d+c_F=2\), that is \(d=1\) and only if \(c_F=1\). The paired source's original instances therefore still cannot serve the goal; they are not excluded as a source for depth one.

What the goal needs

One thing: a degree barrier at half the free dimension, up to \(n^{1-\epsilon}\), for a polynomial cover by affine subspaces. Everything else on the route is proved within the limits recorded in the open statement. The thin-level variant asks the same at half a level-size dimension and is not known to be easier.

Obstacle

No lower-bound method for polynomial calculus over \(\mathbb F_2\) is known to reach half of the free dimension, and no candidate system is known for which such a barrier is even supported by exact computation. The methods in the record are boundary expansion, whose stated bounds stop near a quarter, and static duals, which are necessary conditions. Outside characteristic two the bound \(\lceil n/2\rceil+1\) is known and tight for subset sum (Impagliazzo–Pudlák–Sgall), a symmetric system with one axiom; over \(\mathbb F_2\) a system of that shape, each axiom symmetric, is easy when its axioms have low degree, by the lemma below.

Symmetric systems over the binary field

Lemma (symmetric system ceiling). Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) be symmetric multilinear polynomials over \(\mathbb F_2\) in \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), of degree at most \(d\) with \(1\le d\le(n+1)/2\), with no common zero in \(\{0,1\}^n\). Then they have, with the Boolean axioms, a polynomial calculus refutation of degree at most \(3d-1\).

Proof. Let \(k\ge1\) with \(2^{k-1}\le d<2^k\); then \(2^k\le2d\le n+1\). A symmetric multilinear polynomial of degree at most \(d\) is a combination of \(e_0,\ldots,e_d\), and \(e_j(x)=\binom{|x|}{j}\) modulo two. By Lucas's theorem \(\binom wj\equiv\prod_{i:\,j_i=1}w_i\) for the binary digits, so for \(j<2^k\) the value \(e_j(x)\) is the product of the digits \(b_i=e_{2^i}(x)\), \(i<k\), of \(|x|\) at the positions where \(j\) has a one. Hence \(a_i(x)=A_i(b_0(x),\ldots,b_{k-1}(x))\) for polynomials \(A_i\) on \(\mathbb F_2^k\). Every \(b\in\mathbb F_2^k\) is the digit vector of some weight \(0\le|x|\le n\), because \(2^k\le n+1\); so the \(A_i\) have no common zero on \(\mathbb F_2^k\), and there are functions \(C_i\) on \(\mathbb F_2^k\) with \(\sum_iC_iA_i=1\), for instance \(C_i\) the indicator of the points where \(A_i\) is the first nonzero one. Put \(c_i(x)=C_i(b(x))\), as a multilinear polynomial: a combination of products of distinct \(b_i\), each such product an \(e_j\) with \(j<2^k\), so \(\deg c_i\le2^k-1\). Then \(\sum_ic_ia_i=1\) as functions on the cube, hence as multilinear polynomials. Polynomial calculus derives each monomial multiple \(x_Ta_i\), \(|T|\le2^k-1\), by multiplying by one variable at a time, within degree \(d+2^k-1\le3d-1\), and \(1\) is a combination of these. \(\square\)

What it teaches: a system of individually symmetric axioms that is to be hard at \(n/2-s\) needs \(3d-1\ge n/2-s\), an axiom of degree at least \((n+2)/6-s/3\), outside any budget \(n^{1-\epsilon}\). The subset-sum bound in other characteristics rests on the weight being one linear form; over \(\mathbb F_2\) the weight is seen only through its binary digits, of degrees \(1,2,4,\ldots\), and low-degree symmetric axioms see only the low digits, a problem in logarithmically many variables. Not covered, and not examined: systems invariant only as a set, such as the orbit of a non-symmetric axiom as in the pigeonhole principle, and systems symmetric under a smaller group, such as a product of symmetric groups on blocks.

Architecture review

Necessary target. The covering statement above, for infinitely many \(n\), at \(D=\lfloor n/2-s\rfloor\) with \(s\) and the codimensions at most \(n^{1-\epsilon}\); for one depth \(d\), \(o(n/(\log n)^{d+c_F-2})\). It is equivalent to the open statement, by the encoding proposition and its converse.

Extra requirements. The accepted specification still lists conditions derived for relations on variables: essential scopes, occurrences, no common Horn polarity, joint filtration. They are necessary conditions on the presented CNF, not additional demands, and for rows on dense forms the filtration condition is not binding. The requirement that the family be a polynomial cover by subspaces is the one substantive restriction: a symmetric system with axioms that are not clauses on forms would need its own encoding, with auxiliary variables that count in the dimension unless they are affine.

Independent alternative. Given only the goal, the proved transfer, the covering form and the recorded limits, with the route withheld, the reviewer proposed a static dual witness: a function \(g\) on \(\mathbb F_2^n\) of odd support whose restriction to each subspace of the cover has degree below \(n-D\), then a family of such witnesses stable under the multiplication step, for which it had no construction. The first part is the static unit test already in the record, the odd-mass element of the kernel architecture review and the dual of the sections-dual test: a necessary condition, equivalent to a Nullstellensatz bound. So no architecture materially different from the recorded ones was found. Two of its remarks are kept: by inclusion and exclusion a witness must live on intersections of dimension at most about \(n/2+s\), which points to covers with rich intersection lattices and away from expanding ones; and its smallest test, solving for \(g\) on small covers, is the static counterpart of the decisive test below. Evidence: review.txt.

Rank normalization. The transfer's losses and survivors are measured in one quotient, and its rate needs only level sizes; this was the content of the level-size transfer, and it does not relax the barrier relative to the dimension it uses. For the family statement there is no count to normalize: it is a membership statement, \(1\notin C_D\).

Decision. Keep the covering endpoint. Stop developing leads that restate properness. I had drafted a test of full symmetry with weight arithmetic; the reviewer showed it could not decide anything, and the lemma above disposes of systems of individually symmetric axioms. What is left to learn cheaply is on which side of half the truth lies for small covers, and what extremal covers look like, in the direction the reviewer's remark points: intersections, not expansion.

Decisive test. The hypothesis is the half ceiling in covering form with constant one: every cover of \(\mathbb F_2^n\) by affine subspaces of codimension at most \(w\) is refuted within degree \(\lceil n/2\rceil+w\), the form the product-tree frame satisfied. Test: at \(w=2\) and \(n=7,8\), and larger \(n\) if the exact completion tool allows, with \((n,w)=(7,3),(8,3)\) as secondary cases, compute the polynomial calculus degree of minimal covers, sampled at random and from structured classes (subcube covers, subspaces in general position, covers with many pairwise intersections of dimension near \(n/2\)), and record the largest degree and the covers attaining it. Counted beforehand: against the trivial bound \(n\) the hypothesis leaves slack two at \((7,2)\) and \((8,2)\) and one at \((7,3)\) and \((8,3)\); at \((6,3)\) it is vacuous and that case is not run. The test can refute and cannot support: an instance above \(\lceil n/2\rceil+w\) refutes this form of the ceiling, not the form \(n/2+O(w)\); finding none proves nothing. In either case the covers of largest degree are recorded, and the next step is to state what they have in common and prove a degree bound for that structure in general. This develops the queued ceiling check.

Falsification attempt on this line

Two standard literature searches were made in this cycle, for a general upper bound on polynomial calculus degree near \(n/2\) and for degree lower bounds near half of the variables in characteristic two. They returned the subset-sum and pigeonhole bounds \(\lceil n/2\rceil+1\) with the matching upper bound for subset sum, the linear bounds for random formulas, and nothing stating either a general ceiling at half or a near-half bound over \(\mathbb F_2\). Two searches do not establish absence. The ceiling question stays undecided: if a ceiling \(n/2+O(w)\) holds, the target sits within \(n^{1-\epsilon}\) of the maximum possible, and the family must be nearly extremal.

Checks, scope and verification

Scope. An assessment of this line only. No computation was run. The search results are summaries returned by the search tool, not sources read in full.

Follow-ups whose status changed. Closed or developed in the block: the level-size transfer check, the check on high-degree axioms, two nested checks of the local sections lead, and the nineteen items of the audit. The local sections lead is Continuing at the end of its spell, with its source reread still queued.

9 October 2026 — Small covers by subspaces: exact degrees stay at the codimension plus one, far below half, and say nothing about a ceiling

Finite check with no refutation: at the sizes reachable the hypothesis was never approached, so the test decides nothing about it. Queue development of a chosen check while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Chosen. This check, the base of the ceiling question, bears on the family statement by saying whether the target sits at the maximum possible degree; it comes before the head because the sixth review named it as the decisive test, and the head has only a source reread left.

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: is the half ceiling in covering form, every cover of \(\mathbb F_2^n\) by affine subspaces of codimension at most \(w\) is refuted within degree \(\lceil n/2\rceil+w\), refuted by a small cover? And what do the covers of largest degree look like?

Architecture test. Outcome of the decisive test of the sixth review: not refuted, and uninformative. In 703,500 evaluations of minimal covers at \(n=7\) to \(10\), \(w=2,3\), by sampling and hill climbing in four classes, the largest exact degree reached is \(w+1\), except at \(n=10\), \(w=2\), where nineteen of 140 restarts end at degree \(4\). Only the 3,500 final covers are recorded; first covers often have degree \(w\). The hypothesis allows \(6\) to \(8\). The required implication is unchanged; the route is unchanged; what changes is that searching small covers is not a way to find extremal structure.

New mathematics. None beyond the finite check. A kernel computing the exact degree-\(D\) closure for \(n\le10\) was written and validated against the reference tool.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The family statement is as open as before, and the ceiling question that would say whether its target is extremal is neither supported nor refuted by this check.

General statement. The hypothesis tested is conj:covering-half-ceiling, for all \(n\) and \(w\); it is an untested hypothesis, registered so that it has a name, and this entry gives no evidence for it. The finite check is ex:small-cover-degrees.

Test design, written before the run

Smallest informative parameters: against the trivial bound \(n\), the hypothesis \(\lceil n/2\rceil+w\) leaves slack one at \((n,w)=(7,2)\), two at \((8,2)\) and \((9,2)\), three at \((10,2)\), one at \((8,3)\) and \((9,3)\), and none at \((7,3)\), where it is vacuous. A refutation needs a cover of degree at least \(7\) at \(n=7,8\) and \(w=2\), at least \(8\) at \(n=9,10\) and \(w=2\) and at \(n=8\), \(w=3\), and \(9\) at \(n=9\), \(w=3\). The test can refute and cannot support. My first draft of this paragraph had the slack at \((7,2)\) and \((7,3)\) one too high; the three combinations at \((7,3)\) were run and could not have refuted anything.

Instances: a cover is a list of subspaces \(\{x:\ m_j\cdot x=t_j,\ j<w\}\) of codimension exactly \(w\), with independent masks, its axiom the indicator \(\prod_j(m_j\cdot x+t_j+1)\). Four classes of masks: general (uniform nonzero), subcube (single variables, a \(w\)-CNF), pool (drawn from \(n+2\) to \(2n+2\) fixed random forms, so that subspaces share forms), pairs (sums of at most two variables). Each restart adds random subspaces until the cube is covered, removes redundant ones in random order, and then makes 200 steps of hill climbing: drop one or two subspaces, refill, minimalize, accept if the degree does not fall. The program checks that every reported final instance is a cover and minimal.

Outcome

One run, 23 seconds on 14 threads: 25 parameter and class combinations, 140 restarts each, 28,140 covers evaluated per combination. All reported covers valid. Minimal covers found have 5 to 19 subspaces at \(w=2\) and 10 to 29 at \(w=3\).

\(w\)\(n\)largest degree foundhypothesis
27, 8, 93 (all classes)6, 6, 7
2104 (general class, 19 of 140 restarts; 3 in the other classes)7
37, 8, 94 (all classes)7, 7, 8

Before climbing, subcube covers mostly have degree \(w\) and general covers degree \(w+1\); climbing raises every restart to \(w+1\) and no further, except at \((10,2)\). So at these sizes the degree follows the codimension and not the dimension. It means the sizes are far too small to see either the ceiling or a family approaching it: the test's premise, that extremal structure would show at \(n\le10\), failed. Nothing is learned about the ceiling.

What is learned, for the method: random search with hill climbing over minimal covers does not find degree growing with \(n\) at these sizes in any of the four classes, so a candidate will not come from this kind of sampling at small sizes; and the general class is the only one to reach \(w+2\), at the largest size.

Checks, scope and verification

Validation. The kernel's degree equals that of tools/truncated_buchberger.py on sixteen covers at \(n=6\) from four combinations and, since those use one machine word per polynomial and never reach degree \(w+2\), on eight final covers of the series at \(n=7\) to \(10\), two of them of degree four at \(n=10\); no mismatch in either set. The second set was added at the reviewer's request, who had run six such rows itself. Kernel and scripts: cover_degree.cpp, validate.py. Outputs: series.jsonl (every restart's final cover), validation.txt, validation-multiword.txt, validate-n6.jsonl. Seed 3; command line in the first line of the series file.

Scope. Sampled covers only, biased towards small minimal covers by the way they are generated; not exhaustive at any size. No statement about larger \(n\).

Specification decision. No change. Nothing was excluded or required.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer read the kernel and found no error: leading monomials, multilinear products, the axioms, the early exit, word counts, and that multiplying basis elements suffices; the globals are set before the parallel region. It checked every number against the saved output and confirmed them, and required corrections, applied: two slack values and one impossible threshold in the test design; "degree \(w+1\) in every case" was false, since only final covers are recorded and first covers often have degree \(w\); the validation at \(n=6\) did not exercise polynomials of more than one word, now covered; an uncited sentence about small constants is removed; the claim that the satisfiability question looks hard is replaced by the reduction from three-colouring with its conditional consequence. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing. First entry on this check. The base of the ceiling question is undecided: two literature searches in the review found no statement either way, and this computation cannot reach it. Next attempt on it: the question the data raise at \(w=2\), which covers by subspaces of codimension two need degree growing with \(n\). Some must, unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\): three-colourability of a graph is such a covering question, with two bits per vertex, one forbidden colour and one forbidden difference per edge, and refutations of bounded degree can be searched in polynomial time. The attempt is to read off from that reduction which covers carry the growth and what is recorded about their degree.

Process assessment. The review said beforehand that this test could refute and could not support; it did neither. I chose sizes by what the tool could reach and not by where the hypothesis and the known behaviour differ: with degrees at \(w+1\), a slack of two or three above \(n/2\) was never in play. The cost was small, one 23-second run and a kernel of some hundred lines, but the sixth review's decisive test changed nothing, and that is the second review in a row whose test did so. The series was stopped after one run.

9 October 2026 — A ceiling by conditioning: the degree is at most the rank of forms that make every row affine, plus the width

Working proof of an upper bound generalizing recorded independent-set certificates to rows on forms; it gives the half ceiling for colouring covers and a necessary condition on candidates. Queue development of a chosen check while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Chosen. Second entry on the base of the ceiling question, which bears on the family statement by locating its target relative to the largest possible degree; it comes before the head because the preceding entry left a concrete question on it, and the head has only a source reread left.

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: the preceding entry observed that graph colouring is a cover by subspaces of codimension two. What do the record's colouring results say about such covers, and is there a general reason behind them that applies to every cover?

New mathematics. A general upper bound. If \(T\) is a set of forms such that every row's forms have rank at most one modulo the span of \(T\), then the system is refuted in degree \(\operatorname{rank}T+w\): on each fibre of \(T\) every row is an affine equation, and an inconsistent affine system is refuted in degree one. The record's independent-set bounds for colourings are instances of this pattern, and for the two-bit four-colouring it gives \(N+2=n/2+2\) with \(T\) the first bits. So the half ceiling holds for every system with such a \(T\) of rank at most \(n/2\), and a near-half family must have every such \(T\) of rank above \(n/2-s-w\).

Goal progress. Unchanged. An upper bound and a necessary condition; no family, and the general ceiling question is still undecided.

General statement. prop:transversal-rank-ceiling holds for every unsatisfiable system of clauses on affine forms over \(\mathbb F_2\) and every set \(T\) with the stated property.

Colouring as a cover, and what the record already has

Give each vertex \(v\) of a graph two bits \((x_v,y_v)\). Proper colourings with four colours are the points outside the subspaces \(\{x_u=x_v,\ y_u=y_v\}\), one per edge; forbidding the colour \((1,1)\) by the subspaces \(\{x_v=1,\ y_v=1\}\) gives three colours. So non-colourability is a cover of \(\mathbb F_2^{2N}\) by subspaces of codimension two, with \(n=2N\) and width two. Since three-colourability is NP-complete and refutations of bounded degree can be found in polynomial time, covers of codimension two have unbounded degree unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\); an unconditional statement would need a lower bound for colouring in this encoding, which I did not read for.

The record bounds these from above: thm:compact-colouring-degree-ceiling gives at most \(n/3+4/3\) for three colours, and thm:independent-colour-degree-ceiling gives \(\lfloor3(N-|I|)/2\rfloor+2\) for four colours and any independent set \(I\). Three-colouring covers are therefore excluded as near-half sources, and four-colouring covers need independence number at most about \(N/3\), as already recorded. My first derivation in this cycle, a bound \(3N/4+1\) for three colours from an independent set and a small non-colourable subgraph, is weaker than the recorded theorem and is not registered.

The general bound

Let \(G\) be an unsatisfiable system of clauses on affine forms over \(\mathbb F_2^n\), each clause \((\ell,b)\) on at most \(w\) forms with polynomial \(Q=\prod_j(\ell_j+b_j+1)\), with the Boolean axioms; multilinear representatives throughout.

Proposition (transversal rank ceiling). Let \(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_\rho\) be linearly independent linear forms such that for every clause the linear parts of its forms span a space of dimension at most one modulo \(\operatorname{span}\{\tau_i\}\). Then \(G\) has a polynomial calculus refutation of degree at most \(\rho+w\). (The bound says something only when \(\rho+w<n\); independence of the \(\tau_i\) is used only to call \(\rho\) a rank.)

Proof. For \(a\in\mathbb F_2^\rho\) let \(\chi_a=\prod_i(\tau_i+a_i+1)\), the indicator of the fibre \(\{\tau=a\}\), of degree at most \(\rho\); \(\sum_a\chi_a=1\) as functions and so as multilinear polynomials. Fix \(a\) and a clause. By hypothesis there is a linear form \(\lambda\), zero or outside the span of the \(\tau_i\), with each \(\ell_j\) equal on the fibre to \(\lambda+c_j\) or to a constant \(c_j\). So on the fibre \(Q\) is a product of constants and of forms \(\lambda+c_j+b_j+1\) with one \(\lambda\): it equals \(0\), or \(1\), or one affine form \(\alpha=\lambda+c\), since two such forms with different constants multiply to zero and equal ones to themselves. Hence \(\chi_aQ=\chi_a\alpha_{a}\) as functions, with \(\alpha_a\in\{0,1,\lambda+c\}\) depending on the clause, and so as multilinear polynomials; polynomial calculus derives it from \(Q\) by multiplying by the \(\rho\) factors of \(\chi_a\) one at a time, within degree \(\rho+w\).

The fibre is an affine subspace on which no point satisfies all clauses, that is, on which the affine equations \(\alpha_a=0\) over all clauses have no common solution. An affine system over \(\mathbb F_2\) without solutions has \(1\) in the span of its equations, here the \(\alpha_a\) together with the equations \(\tau_i+a_i\) of the fibre: \(1=\sum_rc_r\alpha_{a,r}+\sum_id_i(\tau_i+a_i)\) with constants. Multiplying by \(\chi_a\) and using \(\chi_a(\tau_i+a_i)=0\) gives \(\chi_a=\sum_rc_r\chi_a\alpha_{a,r}\), a combination of derived polynomials. Summing over \(a\) derives \(1\). \(\square\)

Instances. For clauses on variables, \(T\) is a set of variables containing all but at most one variable of every clause, and the bound is \(n-|U|+w\) for \(U\) a set of variables no two of which share a clause: the pattern of the record's independent-set certificates. For the two-bit four-colouring, \(T\) is the set of first bits: every edge clause has forms \(x_u+x_v\) and \(y_u+y_v\), of rank one modulo the first bits. The three-colour clauses, on the forms \(x_v\) and \(y_v\), also have rank one modulo the first bits, so the same \(T\) serves three colours, with a bound weaker than the recorded \(n/3+4/3\). So every non-four-colourable graph has degree at most \(N+2=n/2+2\) in that encoding, the form \(\lceil n/2\rceil+w\) of conj:covering-half-ceiling; the recorded bound \(\lfloor3(N-|I|)/2\rfloor+2\) is smaller exactly when \(|I|>N/3\). For a cover by subspaces of codimension two, \(T\) may consist of one form from the span of each subspace's two forms.

What it teaches. Write \(\rho(G)\) for the least such rank. A family with no refutation at \(D=\lfloor n/2-s\rfloor\) needs \(\rho(G)\ge D-w+1\): no set of forms of rank well below half makes all rows affine. The two-bit colourings have \(\rho\le n/2\), so their degree is at most \(n/2+2\) and the target is within \(s+2\) of the largest degree they can have; no lower bound on their \(\rho\) is claimed. A lower bound on \(\rho\) in general: \(\operatorname{span}T\) must contain a subspace of codimension at most one of each row's span \(W_i\), so rows whose spans are in direct sum force \(\rho\ge\sum_i(\dim W_i-1)\), about \(n(1-1/w)\), which for \(w=2\) is again \(n/2\). For \(w=2\) and \(m=\beta n\) independent uniformly random two-dimensional row spans, \(\beta>1\), a first-moment count gives \(\rho\ge n-c\) with high probability for every constant \(c>\beta\log_23/(\beta-1)\): there are at most \(4\cdot2^{c(n-c)}\) subspaces of codimension \(c\), each meets a random plane nontrivially with probability at most \(3\cdot2^{-c}\), and \(c(n-c)+2+\beta n(\log_23-c)\to-\infty\). For such systems the proposition says nothing, and whether their degree can exceed \(n/2+w\) is the general question, still open.

Specification decision. Added as a necessary condition, for clauses on forms: \(\rho(G)\ge D-w+1\) when there is no refutation of degree \(D\). It follows from the degree hypothesis, so it excludes nothing the hypothesis allows; it is a screen for candidates, cheap to bound from above by exhibiting one \(T\). It is not vacuous at near-half cutoffs: random dense rows at \(w=2\) meet it by the count above; whether the four-colouring covers meet it depends on a lower bound for their \(\rho\) that is not established. No witness with a near-half barrier is known, as before.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer could not break the proposition or its proof: one residual form per clause, the dependence on the fibre, the three cases, the degree count, the inconsistency criterion with its edge cases, and the final sum. It confirmed the instances, the arithmetic with the floor, the remark on \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), both recorded theorems against their summaries, and that the proposition is neither implied by lem:violated-rows-ceiling nor a restatement of the colouring theorems. Corrections applied: the necessary condition is \(\rho\ge D-w+1\); "nothing to spare" and "exactly at the edge" claimed a lower bound on \(\rho\) for colourings that is not proved; "blocks with one distinguished form per row" was undefined and is removed; "close to \(n\) in general position" was unproved, replaced by the direct-sum bound the reviewer supplied and a first-moment count of mine for random planes, which the reviewer has not checked; the bound is vacuous above \(n-w\); the three-colour instance. Unused: independence of the \(\tau_i\). Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing. Second entry on this check. The ceiling \(\lceil n/2\rceil+w\) is now proved for all systems with \(\rho\le n/2\) and remains undecided in general. Next attempt on it: the proposition is silent where \(\rho>n-w\), which is where random dense rows live, and there the small-cover run found degree \(w+1\) at \(n\le10\); so the attempt is a proof, not a computation: bound the degree of systems with large \(\rho\) by conditioning on fewer forms and paying for non-affine fibres, which is where the earlier splitting induction lost.

Process assessment. I first derived a colouring bound that the record already had in stronger form; the claim search caught it before drafting, and the cycle's result is the general statement behind those bounds instead. No sub-idea is queued; the next attempt is named in the follow-up.

9 October 2026 — Two conditioning inductions fail to give a half ceiling, with the place where each loses

Unsuccessful attempt, obstruction recorded; the ceiling question stays undecided. Queue development of a chosen check while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Chosen. Third entry on the base of the ceiling question, which bears on the family statement by locating its target relative to the largest possible degree; it comes before the head because the preceding entry named this attempt, and the head has only a source reread left.

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: can the transversal rank ceiling be extended to systems whose rows stay non-affine after conditioning, so as to prove conj:covering-half-ceiling or a form of it?

New mathematics. None. Two forms of the conditioning argument are written out with the exact place where each loses, and one reading attempt failed for a technical reason.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The ceiling is neither proved nor refuted.

General statement. The statement attempted is conj:covering-half-ceiling, an untested hypothesis; nothing is established about it here.

Fixed conditioning

Let \(T\) be any set of independent forms of rank \(\rho\), with fibre indicators \(\chi_a\) of degree \(\rho\). On each fibre the system is an unsatisfiable system on a space of dimension \(n-\rho\), with some refutation degree \(d_a\). Lifting as in the proposition, a fibre refutation of degree \(d_a\) gives \(\chi_a\) in degree \(\rho+d_a\), so the degree is at most \(\rho+\max\{w,\max_ad_a\}\), the term \(w\) because deriving \(\chi_aQ\) already costs \(\rho+w\). The proposition is the case \(d_a\le w\) for all fibres. In general, a bound \(d_a\le c(n-\rho)+w\) on fibres, by induction, returns \(\rho+c(n-\rho)+w\), which exceeds \(cn+w\) by \(\rho(1-c)\): for \(c=\tfrac12\) each conditioned form costs half a degree more than the ceiling allows. This is the loss of the earlier splitting attempt. What it shows is that an induction using the worst-case bound on fibres loses for every \(T\): the indicator of a fibre has degree equal to its codimension, while the ceiling grants half of it. A choice of \(T\) that makes the fibres easier than the worst case avoids the loss, as in the proposition.

Adaptive conditioning

For codimension two one can condition adaptively and use that affine consequences are free. Query a form \(\tau\) from the span of a row. On the branch where the row is not yet satisfied, the row becomes an affine equation, and by the free-dimension lemma an affine equation lowers the dimension without cost in degree: that branch pays one degree for two dimensions, the ratio the ceiling needs. On the other branch the row is satisfied and removed, and one degree is paid for one dimension. The strategy that queries one form per row pays, on the path that always takes the second branch, one degree for each independent form queried before the conditions become inconsistent; the forms queried on such a path span at least \(\rho(G)\) dimensions if the path reaches every row, which for random dense rows is \(n-O(1)\) with high probability by the count of the preceding entry. So this strategy does not give a ceiling at half. No lower bound for tree-shaped certificates in general is shown: a tree may query other forms or end early, and systems with large \(\rho\) can have short refutations, as the small-cover run found.

By analogy only: the matching upper bound \(\lceil n/2\rceil+1\) reported for subset sum in large characteristic concerns one linear axiom on \(n\) variables, and I infer, without having read the proof, that it combines cases before their indicators reach full degree.

I tried to read that proof, in Impagliazzo, Pudlák and Sgall's report (ECCC TR97-042), to see how it is organized. The file was retrieved, but its text layer is unreadable, an old font encoding that extracts as symbols, and the journal version is not freely available. The reading is therefore not done; a request for a readable copy is filed with the user.

What the attempt leaves

The half ceiling in covering form is proved for systems with \(\rho\le n/2\), untouched for the rest, and not refuted by any instance; the small computations cannot reach it. These two inductions lose, each at the place stated; other uses of conditioning are not excluded.

Specification decision. No change. Nothing new is necessary or excluded.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer confirmed the lifting and the arithmetic and required corrections, applied: the lifted bound has \(\max\{w,d_a\}\); the loss is shown for an induction with the worst-case fibre bound, not for conditioning as such; my sentence that a tree-shaped certificate cannot beat \(\rho(G)+w\) was false, since systems with large \(\rho\) can have trivial refutations, and only this strategy's worst path is described; the statement about subset sum is labelled inference and analogy; the title and the closing sentence no longer say conditioning is exhausted; the status is Waiting on the source. Record: review.txt.

  • The check waits on a source. Follow-up. Waiting: a readable copy of the Impagliazzo, Pudlák and Sgall upper bound for subset sum, requested in user_requests on 9 October 2026

Follow-up. Continuing. Third entry on this check, which is undecided and now waits on that source. When it is available: read how that proof is organized and try the same on the four-colouring covers, where the bound \(n/2+2\) is the one to beat.

Process assessment. A short cycle with a negative outcome, recorded as such. The item has had three entries, one finite check that could not decide, one general upper bound, and this; it now waits for a source. I drafted a general impossibility for tree-shaped certificates from one strategy's worst path; the reviewer's counterexample was two contradictory unit clauses added to a dense system.

9 October 2026 — The local sections lead read at its source: an anchored compatible family is a static dual condition, weaker than the dual of the system with one local assignment imposed

Source reading, no new result; the lead closes as a restatement at every level examined; twelve of its nested checks are kept by name and three merged into them. Queue development of the head while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: the local sections lead rests on statements of Abramsky, Mansfield and Soares Barbosa that the record had only second-hand. What do they say, and is there anything in them beyond what three entries have found?

New mathematics. None. The source's Section 4 was read in full (arXiv:1111.3620, The Cohomology of Non-Locality and Contextuality), and its anchored condition is translated.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The source supplies a necessary static condition and no method; closing the lead removes an item from the queue and changes nothing in what must be proved.

General statement. No new claim. The translation uses the duality of prop:local-design-criterion as in the sections-dual test.

The statements

For a commutative ring \(R\) the paper forms \(F_R(X)\), finitely supported functions \(X\to R\), with \(F_Rf\) summing coefficients over fibres; it then works with \(R=\mathbb Z\) and the presheaf \(\mathcal F=F_{\mathbb Z}S_e\) of formal integer combinations of local sections in the support of a model \(e\), on a cover by contexts \(C_1,\ldots,C_n\). Fixing a section \(s_1\) on \(C_1\), it defines a class \(\gamma(s_1)\) in a relative cohomology group.

Its Proposition 4.2: \(\gamma(s_1)=0\) if and only if there is a family \(r_i\in\mathcal F(C_i)\) with \(r_1=s_1\) and \(r_i|_{C_i\cap C_j}=r_j|_{C_i\cap C_j}\) for all \(i,j\). Its Proposition 4.3: if the model is possibilistically extendable the obstruction vanishes for every section in the support, and if it is not strongly contextual it vanishes for some section. The paper states that non-vanishing is sufficient and not necessary for contextuality, because of false positives: compatible families that come from no global section.

Translation

Only condition (2) of Proposition 4.2 is translated here, with a cover of my choosing: all sets of at most \(D\) variables, \(|C_1|\le D\), and local sections of a constraint system. The paper's class is defined for the support of a no-signalling model on maximal contexts; local sections of a constraint system need not extend to neighbouring contexts, so the class itself may be undefined in this setting, and nothing below depends on it.

Restriction sums coefficients, so every member of a compatible family has the same total mass; the anchor \(r_1=s_1\) fixes it at one. An anchored family is therefore a mass-one compatible family whose member on \(C_1\) is the single section \(s_1\). In the dictionary of the sections-dual test, with coefficients in a field, it is a functional equal to one at \(1\), vanishing on the multiples of the axioms within degree \(D\), and agreeing with evaluation at \(s_1\) on polynomials in the variables of \(C_1\). By linear duality such a functional exists exactly when \(1\) is not in the span of the axiom multiples within degree \(D\) together with the polynomials on \(C_1\) vanishing at \(s_1\), these last not multiplied by anything. That is implied by, and in general weaker than, the absence of a Nullstellensatz refutation of the system with \(s_1\) imposed, where those polynomials may be multiplied too: with signed coefficients a larger context can carry cancelling weight on assignments that disagree with \(s_1\). For an unsatisfiable system every such family is one of the paper's false positives.

So the criterion of Section 4 is a static dual condition, anchored at a partial assignment: necessary for the degree hypothesis and no more, which is what the first entry on this lead found from the second-hand statement. The reading changes nothing in the three earlier entries. An integer family reduces to a family over every field, so the paper's integer condition is at least as strong as the one over \(\mathbb F_2\) and is still static. I read Section 4 only; the reviewer notes that Sections 6 and 8 contain a divisibility consequence of vanishing over the integers and a completeness conjecture under symmetry, neither of which I read.

The lead's nested checks

All were read in full in the entries that queued them. One is answered by this entry. The other fifteen are separate questions that were nested here because their entries were developing this lead; none is excluded by a recorded result. Twelve are kept, each as its own item, and three that an adjacent item refines are merged into it.

9 October 2026 — A game bound for four-colouring covers: adaptive first-bit queries refute the circular cliques in degree about ten

Working proof of an upper bound by decision trees, and a finite check that excludes at the sizes computed a candidate passing every earlier screen. Queue development of a chosen check while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Chosen. The check on the two-bit four-colour control bears on the family statement directly: a lower bound near the proved ceiling \(n/2+2\) there would be a near-half family in covering form. It comes before the head because the preceding entries made this the one family with a proved half ceiling.

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: which graphs could have a degree barrier at \(N-s\) for the two-bit four-colouring, \(n=2N\)? The record requires independence number at most about \(N/3\); every non-four-colourable induced subgraph on \(W\) vertices gives degree at most \(W+2\), so the graph must also be nearly vertex-critical. The circular cliques \(K_{(4q+1)/q}\) meet both: \(N=4q+1\), independence number \(q\), and every proper induced subgraph four-colourable. Are they candidates?

New mathematics. A third upper bound, by adaptive conditioning: the degree is at most \(\tau(G)+2\), where \(\tau(G)\) is the number of first-bit queries an algorithm needs to force an odd cycle inside one bit class against an adversary. For the circular cliques \(\tau=7\) at \(N=9,13,17\) and \(\tau=8\) at \(N=21,25,29\), by exact search. So these graphs, which pass both earlier screens, have degree at most \(9\) or \(10\) at those sizes, against \(N\) up to \(29\).

Goal progress. Unchanged. A candidate class is tested and fails from \(q=4\) at the sizes computed; a new necessary condition is recorded. No family is obtained and the required implication is as before.

General statement. prop:first-bit-game-ceiling holds for every non-four-colourable graph. The finite check is ex:circular-clique-game-values; that \(\tau\) of the circular cliques stays far below \(N\) for all \(q\) is not proved.

The game and the bound

Encoding as in the transversal rank entry: bits \((x_v,y_v)\) per vertex, one axiom \((x_u+x_v+1)(y_u+y_v+1)\) per edge. The game on a graph \(G\): the algorithm names a vertex not yet queried; the adversary puts it in class \(0\) or \(1\) so that both classes of queried vertices induce bipartite graphs; when neither class is possible the algorithm has won. Let \(\tau(G)\) be the number of queries, the winning one included, under optimal play. If \(G\) is not four-colourable the algorithm wins by the time all vertices are queried, so \(\tau(G)\le N\).

Proposition (first-bit game ceiling). For a graph \(G\) that is not four-colourable, the two-bit four-colouring system has a polynomial calculus refutation over \(\mathbb F_2\) of degree at most \(\tau(G)+2\).

Proof. An optimal strategy is a decision tree of depth \(\tau\) querying the bits \(x_v\). Extend it to all assignments of the bits: at any node, an answer the adversary could not legally give closes an odd cycle inside one class of the queried set, and that child is made a leaf; at the last query of a path both answers do. So every leaf \(\lambda\) is reached by answers \(a\) on a set \(Q_\lambda\) of at most \(\tau\) vertices such that some class \(\{v\in Q_\lambda:\ a_v=c\}\) contains an odd cycle \(C_\lambda\), and every assignment reaches a leaf. Optimality is not needed: any winning tree of depth \(t\) gives \(t+2\). Let \(\chi_\lambda=\prod_{v\in Q_\lambda}(x_v+a_v+1)\), of degree at most \(\tau\). For an edge \(uv\) of \(C_\lambda\), \(x_u=x_v\) on the support of \(\chi_\lambda\), so \(\chi_\lambda(x_u+x_v+1)(y_u+y_v+1)=\chi_\lambda(y_u+y_v+1)\) as functions and as multilinear polynomials, derived from the edge axiom by multiplying by the factors of \(\chi_\lambda\) one at a time within degree \(\tau+2\). Summing over the edges of \(C_\lambda\), each \(y_v\) occurs twice and the constants sum to \(|C_\lambda|\), odd: the sum is \(\chi_\lambda\). The leaves partition the assignments of the \(x\)-bits, so \(\sum_\lambda\chi_\lambda=1\). \(\square\)

The bound with all first bits conditioned, \(N+2\), is the case of a tree that queries every vertex. The proposition is the adaptive form whose worst path the preceding entry could only describe; here the affine system on a leaf is one odd cycle, so the tree's depth is the whole cost. For the join of an odd cycle with an edge \(\tau=N\): the adversary puts the edge vertices in class \(0\) and cycle vertices in class \(1\), except that a cycle vertex which would complete the cycle goes to class \(0\) when at most one edge vertex has been queried; this survives \(N-1\) queries in every order. That graph has independence number \((N-3)/2\) and falls to the recorded independent-set bound instead. So the game bound alone does not exclude every graph, and the circular cliques below show that the independent-set bound alone does not either.

The circular cliques

\(K_{(4q+1)/q}\) has vertices \(\mathbb Z_p\), \(p=4q+1\), with \(i\sim j\) when the circular distance is at least \(q\). It is not four-colourable, since independent sets have at most \(q\) vertices and \(4q<N\); and deleting a vertex leaves four blocks of \(q\) consecutive vertices, each independent, so every vertex-deleted subgraph is four-colourable. The exact program also asserts both by enumeration for \(q\le4\). Hypothesis tested, stated before the run: \(\tau\ge N-c\) for a constant \(c\), which the family needs in order to survive the proposition. Prediction count: at \(N=13\) and \(17\) the hypothesis asks for values near \(12\) and \(16\); a value of at most \(N/2\) at both refutes it at those sizes.

\(q\)1234567
\(N=4q+1\)591317212529
\(\tau\)5777888
degree at most7999101010

By the stated criterion, \(\tau\le N/2\), the hypothesis is refuted at every size from \(q=4\); at \(q=3\) the value \(7\) is just above \(N/2\), and at \(q=2\) it is \(N-2\). The values grow slowly with \(q\). Heuristically, an adversary answering by a pattern of four arcs with an unknown rotation should survive about \(\log_2q\) queries, so I expect growth of that order; neither the heuristic nor the expectation is a result. No bound for all \(q\) is proved. The series is stopped here: larger sizes would not change the conclusion at the sizes that matter for a candidate, and a statement for all \(q\) needs a proof.

What the exclusion teaches: near vertex-criticality and small independence number are properties of the graph offline, while a refutation may query adaptively; a graph can have all proper subgraphs four-colourable and still lose the online game in a few moves, because the adversary must commit each vertex before seeing the rest. A candidate must let the adversary keep both classes bipartite online for \(N-s-2\) queries against every query order.

Checks, scope and verification

Kernels. Two independent programs: an exact minimax over all states for \(N\le17\), with a table of bipartite subsets, and a bounded search with a transposition table and bipartiteness computed directly, for \(N\le29\). They agree at \(q=2,3,4\). \(K_5\) gives \(5\), as it must. A control: on windows of the sequence \(jq\bmod p\) with the adjacency rule valid for small index differences, which are four-colourable, the exact program reports that the adversary survives every query. Sources: bit_game.cpp, bit_game_bounded.cpp; outputs exact.txt (with an optimal strategy tree for each \(q\le4\)) and bounded.txt. All runs took seconds.

Scope. Game values are exact for the sizes listed. The degree bound is an upper bound; the true degree may be smaller. Nothing is claimed for \(q\ge8\).

Specification decision. For candidates of the two-bit four-colouring kind, a necessary condition is added: \(\tau(G)\ge D-1\) when there is no refutation of degree \(D\), beside the recorded bound on the independence number and near vertex-criticality. It follows from the degree hypothesis and excludes nothing the hypothesis allows. It is binding: at a cutoff \(D=N-s\) with \(s\) small, the circular cliques pass the other two conditions and fail this one from \(q=3\) on, where \(\tau+2<N-2\). No graph is known to pass all three at near-half cutoffs.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer checked the proposition, both kernels and the table against the saved outputs and found them sound: the identity, the degree count, the cycle sum, the exactness of the minimax with its short-circuits, the bounded search with its table bounds and first-move symmetry, and the window rule. Corrections applied: the proof now says why illegal answers at inner nodes are leaves, so that the tree covers every assignment; the adversary for the join example is stated completely; the reasons for non-four-colourability and vertex-criticality are given for all \(q\), since only one program asserts them; my counts of refuting sizes were wrong against my own criterion and are corrected; the heuristic about arcs is marked as such. Unused: optimality of the strategy. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing. First entry on this check. The lower side asked for by the check is not obtained; what is obtained narrows where it could hold. Next attempt on it: decide whether the two upper bounds together exclude every graph, that is, whether a non-four-colourable graph with independence number at most \(N/3+o(N)\) can have \(\tau\ge N-o(N)\); the join shows the game bound alone does not, and the circular cliques show the independent-set bound alone does not.

Process assessment. The candidate came from asking what the two recorded screens leave, and it was dead within the cycle by a bound that is one paragraph of proof. The computation was sized to the question, seconds, and stopped once the hypothesis had failed by its criterion at four sizes, \(q=4\) to \(7\). No sub-idea is queued.

9 October 2026 — The circular cliques are refuted in logarithmic degree, for every size

Working proof for all parameters, replacing the finite check of the preceding entry as the reason this family is excluded; the question whether any graph passes all three screens stays open. Queue development of a chosen check while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Chosen. Second entry on the two-bit four-colour check, which bears on the family statement as the one encoding with a proved half ceiling; it comes before the head because the preceding entry left a named question on it.

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: the preceding entry computed the game value of the circular cliques \(K_{(4q+1)/q}\) for \(q\le7\) and proved nothing for larger \(q\). Is the value small for every \(q\)? And can a graph have small independence number and large game value together?

New mathematics. For every \(q\ge1\) the game value of \(K_{(4q+1)/q}\) is at most \(\lceil\log_2q\rceil+6\), so its two-bit four-colouring is refuted in degree at most \(\lceil\log_2q\rceil+8\), against \(N=4q+1\). The strategy is a bisection for two neighbouring positions in different classes, followed by three queries. The second question is not answered.

Goal progress. Unchanged. One family is excluded for all sizes from \(q=3\); no family is obtained, the required implication is as before, and the general question about the three screens is open.

General statement. thm:circular-clique-degree-bound holds for every \(q\ge1\).

The bound

\(G_q=K_{(4q+1)/q}\): vertices \(\mathbb Z_p\), \(p=4q+1\), with \(i\sim j\) when the circular distance \(\min\{|i-j|,p-|i-j|\}\) is at least \(q\). The game and \(\tau\) are as in the preceding entry.

Theorem (circular clique degree bound). For every \(q\ge1\), \(\tau(G_q)\le\lceil\log_2q\rceil+6\), and the two-bit four-colouring system of \(G_q\) has a polynomial calculus refutation over \(\mathbb F_2\) of degree at most \(\lceil\log_2q\rceil+8\).

Proof. The second statement follows from the first by prop:first-bit-game-ceiling. For the first, describe a strategy; at any point where the adversary has no legal answer the algorithm has won, so assume legal answers throughout.

Step 1. Query \(0,q,2q\). They are pairwise at circular distance \(q\), \(q\) and \(2q\), so they form a triangle and do not all receive the same class. Hence for \(i=0\) or \(i=1\) the vertices \(iq\) and \((i+1)q\) are in different classes.

Step 2. The positions \(iq,iq+1,\ldots,(i+1)q\) form an interval of \(q+1\) consecutive positions whose endpoints are in different classes. Bisect: query the middle position of the current interval and keep a half whose endpoints differ. After at most \(\lceil\log_2q\rceil\) queries there is a position \(c\) such that \(c-1\) and \(c\) are queried and in different classes.

Step 3. Query \(c+q\), \(c+2q\), \(c+3q\), unless already queried. These three are pairwise at circular distance \(q\), \(q\), \(2q\): a triangle. The vertex \(c\) is at circular distance \(q\), \(2q\) and \(q+1\) from them, and \(c-1\) at distance \(q+1\), \(2q\) and \(q\); so both are adjacent to all three. If two of the three were in the class of \(c\), they would form a triangle with \(c\) inside that class; likewise for \(c-1\). So each class may receive at most one of the three, and the third has no legal class. The adversary is stuck by the last of these queries.

The total is at most \(3+\lceil\log_2q\rceil+3\). Vertices of Step 3 queried earlier only shorten the play, since the argument uses their classes and not the order. \(\square\)

Against the exact values: the bound gives \(7,8,8,9,9,9\) for \(q=2,\ldots,7\), where the search found \(7,7,7,8,8,8\); for \(q=1\) it gives \(6\) and the value is \(5\).

What it teaches

For \(q\ge2\) the five vertices \(c-1,c,c+q,c+2q,c+3q\) induce a complete graph minus the edge between \(c-1\) and \(c\); for \(q=1\) they are all of \(K_5\). In any graph, the two non-adjacent vertices of such a configuration must be in the same class once all five are queried: the mechanism of Step 3. In \(G_q\) these configurations link every position to its neighbour, so legal play would make the class constant along the circle, which a triangle forbids; bisection finds the break in logarithmically many queries. The family's symmetry and density, which gave it small independence number, also gave the algorithm this chain.

The general question is open. A graph that is to pass all three screens needs independence number at most about \(N/3\), all large induced subgraphs four-colourable, and an online adversary surviving nearly \(N\) queries. One mechanism that must then be absent is the one used here: cheap queries that force two vertices into different classes, such as a triangle, joined by a short chain of configurations each forcing its pair into the same class. The only graphs in the record with large game value are joins of a long odd cycle with an edge, with independence number about \(N/2\). I tried the joins of a bipartite graph having an edge with an odd cycle as an intermediate family: they contain the join of the cycle with one edge, a non-four-colourable subgraph on fewer vertices, so they fail near-criticality and teach nothing new. I have no argument that small independence number forces a small game value, and no graph with both.

Specification decision. No change beyond the condition added in the preceding entry. The circular cliques are now excluded by a theorem for every \(q\ge3\), where \(\lceil\log_2q\rceil+8<N-2\); at \(q=1,2\) the bound is not below \(N\). Before, they were excluded at computed sizes only.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer checked the theorem by hand for every \(q\ge1\), with \(q=1,2,3\) separately: the three steps, all nine distances of Step 3, distinctness of the five vertices, the two possible repeats among queried vertices, the count and the comparison with the exact values; no change to the proof. Corrections applied to the prose: the configuration is a complete graph minus an edge only for \(q\ge2\); my sentence about chains between adjacent vertices was wrong, since forcing adjacent vertices into one class is legal, and is replaced by the mechanism actually used; the join remark needs the bipartite graph to have an edge; the exclusion holds from \(q=3\). Unused: non-adjacency of \(c-1\) and \(c\); the third query of Step 1 when the first two already differ. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing. Second entry on this check. Next attempt on it: the general question in a form that can be attacked, whether near vertex-criticality with independence number at most \(N/3\) forces a chain of forcing configurations, starting from what vertex-critical five-chromatic graphs with small independence number are known.

Process assessment. The preceding entry stopped the computation and said a statement for all sizes needed a proof; the proof came from reading the optimal strategies the program printed, whose first branch already used a complete graph minus an edge. A scheduled review is due next.

9 October 2026 — Goal-level review: upper bounds are cheap and no lower-bound method exists; the colouring frame as the place to test what a candidate must be

Goal-level route review: one open statement, unchanged across thirteen research entries. No outside leads or bridges while the queue drains. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: twelve research entries since the fifth review, and thirteen in all since the transfer was proved, have not changed the open statement. What did they obtain, what does that pattern say about the route, and what should the next cycle test?

Architecture test. The decisive test of the sixth review, exact degrees of small covers against a ceiling at half, was carried out and decided nothing: degrees stayed at the codimension plus one. The block then went where that test pointed by accident, to colouring covers, and obtained real statements there.

New mathematics. One example, in the falsification attempt: a ring of gadgets that passes the three screens of the block and is nevertheless refuted in constant degree, through affine equations that each gadget implies. It shows that the count of free dimensions must be taken after such implied equations.

Goal progress. Unchanged. The open statement is the same as at the fifth review. The block's results are upper bounds, necessary conditions and exclusions.

General statement. The goal is the conjunction of thm:near-half-frege-transfer, proved, with the open family statement in the covering form of prop:form-clause-encoding.

Across the goal

  • Near-half Boolean PC family: open, status unchanged since the last goal-level review; six research cycles in this block, twelve since the fifth review.
  • Complete Frege transfer: working proof within stated limits since the fifth review; no cycle spent on it in this block. Its constant \(c_F\) is still not computed, which matters only for the lowest level count.

The block's results, with claim IDs. A general upper bound by conditioning, prop:transversal-rank-ceiling: degree at most the rank of forms that make every row affine, plus the width; it proves the half ceiling for two-bit four-colouring, \(n/2+2\). Two inductions that fail to extend it. The adaptive form for colourings, prop:first-bit-game-ceiling: degree at most the value of an online game plus two. The exclusion of the circular cliques, first at computed sizes, ex:circular-clique-game-values, then for all sizes in logarithmic degree, thm:circular-clique-degree-bound. The closure of the local sections lead as a restatement, after its source was read. From the sixth review: lem:symmetric-system-ceiling. One finite check that could not decide its question, ex:small-cover-degrees.

The auxiliary session sent an exchange note on 9 October 2026. It imported the Kruskal–Katona growth lemma from here and offered three results; none bears on the family statement as it stands, by that note's own account: a closure criterion for quotients built from moment data, a cost bound for covers that does not lift multiplication, and an import on general proof systems over finite fields that does not replace the degree hypothesis.

Obstacle

The same as at the last three reviews, and now with a pattern around it. There is no method for proving a polynomial calculus degree lower bound over \(\mathbb F_2\) near half of the free dimension, and none of the cycles since the transfer produced a step towards one. What the cycles do produce, reliably and within one cycle each, is upper bounds: every candidate examined in this block and the last fell to a bound with a short proof: symmetric systems, the circular cliques, and the ring below; three-colouring had fallen earlier, by thm:compact-colouring-degree-ceiling. Each bound became a necessary condition. The conditions accumulate and no object is known to meet them; that is evidence that candidates of the kinds tried are easy, and no evidence about whether the target is attainable.

Architecture review

Necessary target. Unchanged: for infinitely many \(n\), polynomially many affine subspaces of codimension at most \(n^{1-\epsilon}\) covering \(\mathbb F_2^n\), with no refutation within \(n^{1-\epsilon}\) of degree \(n/2\).

Extra requirements. The block worked inside one encoding, two-bit four-colouring, where the half ceiling is proved and the target is the largest degree the encoding allows. That restriction is a choice, not a requirement: it was made because it is the only family in the record with a proved ceiling at half, so that the question "can the target be met" is sharp there. A family elsewhere would do as well.

Independent alternative. Given the goal, the covering form, the list of upper bounds and the fact that thirteen cycles changed nothing, with the route withheld, the reviewer proposed to work in the static dual and to aim it at the half ceiling instead of at more candidates. Its object, an odd-weight function whose restriction to each subspace has low degree, is the static unit test already in the record, as at the sixth review. Three of its points are new to the record and kept as the reviewer's unverified remarks: by inclusion and exclusion such a function must live on intersections of codimension above \(D\), which is what the rank and subgraph bounds detect; a lower-bound method must be global, must use overlaps of the subspaces and must be invariant under affine maps; and a ceiling at half for width two might be provable from the fact that every Boolean function has a nonzero annihilator of degree at most \(\lceil n/2\rceil\), a mechanism that is not conditioning. It found no endpoint avoiding the threshold at half. It also asked whether the codimension budget \(n^{1-\epsilon}\) is the right convention, since polynomially many subspaces can cover only if nearly all of the measure lies in subspaces of codimension \(O(\log n)\); the budget is what the transfer allows, and the record has only the weaker fact that some member has codimension at most \(\log_2m\). Its proposed search for a small instance of degree above \(n/2\) at width two is already answered for random instances by ex:parity-two-clause-exact-degree and ex:small-cover-degrees. I did not have the reviewer verify that its object coincides with the recorded unit test; that identification is mine. Evidence: review.txt.

Rank normalization. Not applicable to the family statement, a membership statement \(1\notin C_D\); for the transfer it was settled by the level-size form.

Decision. Keep the covering endpoint. The reviewer, shown the route, recommends the ceiling at width two first, since it bears on the route's viability while more work in the colouring frame yields only further exclusions; I adopt that order. The colouring frame has given three bounds and a correction to how dimensions are counted, and no object; it is not continued until the ceiling attempt is made. Neither is a lower-bound method. I have no proposal for one, and say so.

Decisive test. Attempt to prove a ceiling for width two: every unsatisfiable system of products of two affine forms over \(\mathbb F_2^n\), with the Boolean axioms, has a polynomial calculus refutation of degree at most \(cn+O(1)\), using that every Boolean function has a nonzero annihilator of degree at most \(\lceil n/2\rceil\), a mechanism that is not conditioning. Outcomes: a proof with \(c<\tfrac12\) excludes every width-two cover, the graph-colouring covers among them, and the specification must then require growing width; a proof with \(c=\tfrac12\) only says that the target is the maximum for width two, as it already is for four-colouring; no proof, with the step that fails named, leaves the question where it is and the next cycle returns to the queue. A system of width two with degree above \(n/2+O(1)\) would refute conj:covering-half-ceiling in its constant-one form; none is known and the recorded computations make one unlikely at reachable sizes.

Falsification attempt on this line

The preceding entry left open whether a graph can pass the three screens for two-bit four-colouring together: independence number at most about \(N/3\), every proper induced subgraph four-colourable, and game value near \(N\). It can. Take terminals \(t_0,\ldots,t_k\) and triangles \(\Delta_1,\ldots,\Delta_k\), join every vertex of \(\Delta_i\) to \(t_{i-1}\) and \(t_i\), and add the edge \(t_0t_k\): a ring of \(k\) copies of the complete graph on five vertices minus an edge, \(N=4k+1\).

  • Not four-colourable: in a partition into two bipartite classes each gadget forces \(t_{i-1}\) and \(t_i\) into one class, which then contains exactly one vertex of \(\Delta_i\), adjacent to both; so one class contains the cycle \(t_0,a_1,t_1,\ldots,a_k,t_k\) closed by the edge \(t_kt_0\), of length \(2k+1\).
  • Every vertex-deleted subgraph is four-colourable: put the terminals and one vertex of each remaining complete triangle in class \(0\), the other triangle vertices in class \(1\); with a vertex deleted the long cycle is broken, class \(0\) is a union of paths and class \(1\) a matching.
  • Independence number \(k=(N-1)/4\): a triangle contributes at most one vertex and then excludes its two terminals, so \(s\ge1\) contributing triangles exclude at least \(s+1\) terminals and leave at most \(s+(k+1)-(s+1)=k\); with \(s=0\) the terminals give \(k\), since \(t_0,t_k\) are adjacent.
  • Game value \(N\): the adversary puts terminals in class \(0\) and, in each triangle, the first two vertices queried in class \(1\) and the third in class \(0\). Class \(1\) is a matching and class \(0\) a subgraph of the long cycle, proper until the last vertex of the graph is queried.

So the three bounds of the block give nothing below \(N\) for this ring: the independence bound is \(\lfloor3(3k+1)/2\rfloor+2>N\), and the subgraph and game bounds are \(N+2\).

It is refuted in constant degree all the same, by an argument the reviewer supplied. In a proper four-colouring of a gadget the triangle uses three colours and both terminals are adjacent to all of it, so the terminals have the same colour: the gadget's axioms imply \(x_{t_{i-1}}+x_{t_i}=0\) and \(y_{t_{i-1}}+y_{t_i}=0\). These are consequences of axioms on ten bits, and any consequence of a system on \(b\) Boolean variables is derivable within degree \(b+2\), all polynomials there having degree at most \(b\). Summing the equations around the ring, in degree one, gives \(x_{t_0}=x_{t_k}\) and \(y_{t_0}=y_{t_k}\), and the axiom of the edge \(t_0t_k\) becomes \(1\). The degree is at most twelve for every \(k\).

What this teaches is not a new kind of bound but a correction to the count. The ring has \(n=2N\) bits and \(2k\) affine equations derivable in constant degree; by the free-dimension lemma they are free, and after them the terminals are one vertex and the system is a bouquet of gadgets on \(6k+2\) free bits, each gadget contradicting nothing by itself and the one edge contradicting the collapsed terminal. The three screens were computed in the original count. A candidate must be judged after all affine consequences of low degree have been taken out: its free dimension is the dimension that remains. The online game does not see this, because it conditions on bits and never uses an implied equation.

Checks, scope and verification

Scope. An assessment of the whole goal's one open statement. No computation was run for this entry. The ring's four properties and its constant degree are proved above in outline and checked by the reviewer, who supplied the degree argument.

Follow-ups whose status changed. Closed: the local sections lead, with twelve nested checks kept and three merged. Waiting on a source requested from the user: the base of the ceiling question. Continuing: the four-colour control check, two entries.

Verification gate. One medium reviewer in the staged form. Stage one, with the route withheld, is recorded above. Stage two verified the ring's four properties by hand, including the small cases and every possible last vertex of the game, and then settled the ring's degree with an argument I had not seen, so that one outcome of my drafted decisive test could not occur; it found that test not well posed, a hypothesis about "some small separator structure" being unfalsifiable and aimed at the wrong generalization, and recommended the ceiling at width two first. The decision and the test are rewritten accordingly. It also had me cite three-colouring correctly, list the finite check on circular cliques, and record its query on the codimension budget. Record: review.txt.

Process assessment. Two reviews in a row named decisive tests that decided nothing; the useful work of this block came from following a concrete encoding with a proved ceiling. The queue rules changed during the block at the user's direction: order chosen by bearing, batching and merging of sub-ideas, thresholds of thirty and ten, parentless sub-ideas held for review; none waits now. The reviewer corrected an overstatement or an error in every entry of the block, and twice a false general claim; I draft too broadly from one case; in this review the reviewer settled in a paragraph an example whose degree I had left as an expectation.

Decision. Core: the near-half Boolean PC family remains the statement worked on, the only open one. Next cycle: the decisive test above, as a research entry developing a queued check on products of two affine forms, chosen for its bearing on that statement.

9 October 2026 — Annihilators give low-degree members of the ideal, not of the closure: no ceiling at width two obtained from them

Unsuccessful attempt with the failing step named; the ceiling at width two stays undecided. Queue development of a chosen check while draining. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort low).

Chosen. The check on the degree of products of two affine forms bears on the family statement by deciding whether width-two covers can reach half at all; it comes before the head because the goal-level review named it as the decisive test.

Question. On near-half-family and the Boolean PC family statement: is every unsatisfiable system of products of two affine forms over \(\mathbb F_2^n\) refuted within degree \(cn+O(1)\) with \(c=\tfrac12\) or less, provably from the fact that every Boolean function has a nonzero annihilator of degree at most \(\lceil n/2\rceil\)?

Architecture test. Outcome of the decisive test of the goal-level review: the third of its outcomes, no proof. For a subset of the axioms, when the first alternative of the annihilator fact holds, it produces a polynomial of degree at most \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) in the ideal they generate; nothing makes it derivable within that degree, and the gap between membership in the ideal and membership in the degree-bounded closure is the statement to be proved. The dual form of the attempt reduces to a parity condition that covers satisfy easily. The route is unchanged and the next cycle returns to the queue.

New mathematics. None. One remark from the review's reviewer is proved, as a necessary condition for a static dual witness.

Goal progress. Unchanged. No ceiling and no counterexample; the question whether width-two covers can reach half is where it was.

General statement. The statement attempted is the width-two case of conj:covering-half-ceiling, an untested hypothesis; nothing is established about it.

The direct form

Let the axioms be \(Q_i=f_ig_i\), indicators of subspaces \(A_i\) of codimension two covering \(\mathbb F_2^n\). For \(j\le m\) let \(S_j\) be the set of points outside \(A_1,\ldots,A_j\), so \(S_m=\emptyset\). The annihilator fact, applied to the indicator of \(S_j\) or its complement, gives a nonzero \(u\) of degree at most \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) vanishing on \(S_j\) or on its complement. In the first case \(u\) lies in the ideal generated by \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_j\) and the Boolean axioms, which is radical and so is the ideal of all functions vanishing on \(S_j\); the second case gives only the identities \(uQ_i=0\). That is all the fact gives, and at \(j=m\), where a refutation is wanted, the ideal contains \(1\) and the fact is vacuous. To use \(u\) in a refutation of degree about \(n/2\) one needs \(u\) in the degree-\(D\) closure of those axioms for \(D\) near \(n/2\): a representation \(u=\sum_ip_iQ_i\) exists, but the \(p_i\) have no degree bound, and an induction on \(j\) that would supply one is the ceiling itself for the subsystem. I found no way to choose \(u\) so that derivability comes with it, and neither did the reviewer, asked to try; the fact is a statement about dimensions of spaces of functions and knows nothing about how the ideal is generated.

The dual form

If there is no refutation of degree \(D\), there is in particular no static one, and so a function \(h\) of odd weight with \(\deg(h|_{A_i})\le n-D-1\) on every \(A_i\), as recorded. One might hope that for \(D\) above \(n/2\) the degree bounds on a cover force even weight.

Remark. Let affine subspaces \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) cover \(\mathbb F_2^n\) and let \(h\) have \(\deg(h|_{A_i})\le r\) for all \(i\). If \(h\) has odd weight, then some nonempty intersection \(A_T=\bigcap_{i\in T}A_i\) has dimension at most \(r\).

Proof. A point lying in exactly \(k\ge1\) of the subspaces lies in \(A_T\) for \(2^k-1\) nonempty sets \(T\), an odd number; so the weight of \(h\) is congruent modulo two to the sum over nonempty \(T\) with \(A_T\ne\emptyset\) of the weight of \(h|_{A_T}\). The weight of a function on an affine space of dimension \(e\) is odd exactly when its degree there is \(e\), and \(\deg(h|_{A_T})\le\deg(h|_{A_i})\le r\) for \(i\in T\). So every term with \(\dim A_T>r\) is even. \(\square\)

With \(r=n-D-1\) the condition asks for a nonempty intersection of codimension at least \(D+1\). For width two that needs at least \((D+1)/2\), about \(n/4\), subspaces through a common point whose forms have joint rank at least \(D+1\); a cover with \(m\) subspaces has mean multiplicity \(m/4\), so this is available once \(m\) exceeds about \(n\) and the forms are spread. So the parity argument bounds the static degree by the largest codimension of a nonempty intersection, excludes only covers whose intersections are all large, such as partitions into cosets, and gives no ceiling. It does say where a static witness must be supported, as the reviewer remarked.

What the attempt leaves

Three attempts at a ceiling have now failed, each at the same kind of step: splitting, conditioning and annihilators all produce objects in the full ideal or on fibres, and each needs the bounded-degree derivability it set out to prove. The computations on record, sampled covers up to \(n=10\) and random products up to \(n=28\), find no width-two system of degree above \(n/2\) and cannot reach sizes where one would show. Undecided.

Specification decision. No change. No outcome of the test that would have required growing width occurred.

Verification gate. One fresh-context medium reviewer found the mathematics sound, tried and failed to make the annihilator fact give derivability, and required corrections, applied: the fact gives an ideal member only in its first alternative and is vacuous for the whole system; the sentence that any cover with a few subspaces through a point meets the parity condition was overstated, the need being about \(n/4\) subspaces through a point with forms of rank above \(D\); the title read as an impossibility result; the constant in the question, the earlier attempts and the computations are now stated and linked. Unused: width two in the remark, which is stated in general. Record: review.txt.

Follow-up. Continuing. First entry on this check. Its question for random systems and the ceiling for all width-two systems are both open. Next attempt on it: a lower bound instead of a ceiling, on the one width-two family with structure and a proved upper bound at half, two-bit four-colouring with degree at most \(n/2+2\) by prop:transversal-rank-ceiling, for a graph without low-degree affine consequences; first decide which graphs have none.

Process assessment. The third decisive test in a row to end without changing anything. The two ceiling attempts and this one cost a cycle each and returned the same obstruction in three forms; the next review should weigh whether the ceiling question deserves further cycles before the source on subset sum is read.
